sentences.zh: 仁宗十子。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong had ten sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong had ten sons.

sentences.zh: 昭皇后生宣宗、越王瞻墉、襄王瞻墡。

translations.literal: Empress Zhao gave birth to Emperor Xuanzong, the Prince of Yue Zhan Yong, and the Prince of Xiang Zhan Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhao bore Emperor Xuanzong, the Prince of Yue Zhan Yong, and the Prince of Xiang Zhan Fan.

sentences.zh: 李賢妃生鄭王瞻飐、蘄王瞻垠、淮王瞻墺。

translations.literal: Consort Li the Worthy gave birth to the Prince of Zheng Zhan Fei, the Prince of Qi Zhan Yin, and the Prince of Huai Zhan Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Li the Worthy bore the Prince of Zheng Zhan Fei, the Prince of Qi Zhan Yin, and the Prince of Huai Zhan Ao.

sentences.zh: 張順妃生荊王蟾堈。

translations.literal: Consort Zhang the Compliant gave birth to the Prince of Jing Chan Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang the Compliant bore the Prince of Jing, Zhan Kan.

sentences.zh: 郭貴妃生滕王瞻塏、梁王瞻垍、衛王瞻埏。

translations.literal: Consort Guo the Honored gave birth to the Prince of Teng Zhan Kai, the Prince of Liang Zhan Ji, and the Prince of Wei Zhan Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Guo the Honored bore the Prince of Teng Zhan Kai, the Prince of Liang Zhan Ji, and the Prince of Wei Zhan Yan.

sentences.zh: 鄭靖王瞻飐，仁宗第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Zheng, Zhan Fei, was the second son of Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Zheng, Zhan Fei, was Emperor Renzong's second son.

sentences.zh: 永樂二十二年十月封。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-second year of Yongle he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the tenth month of Yongle 22.

sentences.zh: 仁宗崩，皇后命與襄王監國，以待宣宗，宣德元年，帝征樂安，仍命與襄王居守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong died, the empress ordered him and the Prince of Xiang to supervise the state and await Emperor Xuanzong; in the first year of Xuande, when the emperor campaigned against Le'an, he was again ordered with the Prince of Xiang to remain and guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong died, the empress ordered him and the Prince of Xiang to supervise the realm until Xuanzong arrived. In Xuande 1, when the emperor marched against Le'an, the two princes were again left to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年就藩鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went to his fief at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he took up his fief at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 正統八年詔遷懷慶，留京邸，明年之國。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhengtong an edict moved his fief to Huaiqing; he remained at his capital residence, and the next year went to his state.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 8 an edict transferred his fief to Huaiqing. He stayed at his residence in the capital and went to his princedom the following year.

sentences.zh: 蟾飐暴歷，數斃人杖下。

translations.literal: Chan Fei was violent and cruel and often beat people to death under the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Fei was brutal and tyrannical, and many died under his beatings.

sentences.zh: 英宗以御史周瑛為長史，稍戢。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong appointed censor Zhou Ying as chief steward, and he was somewhat restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong appointed the censor Zhou Ying as his chief steward, and the prince was somewhat curbed.

sentences.zh: 成化二年薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chenghua 2.

sentences.zh: 子簡王祁锳嗣。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Jian Qi Rang, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi Rang, Prince Jian, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 祁锳之為世子也，襄王朝京師，經新鄉，祁锳不請命，遣長史往迎。

translations.literal: When Qi Rang was heir apparent, the Prince of Xiang came to court at the capital and passed through Xinxiang; Qi Rang did not request permission but sent his chief steward to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: While Qi Rang was still heir apparent, the Prince of Xiang came to the capital and passed through Xinxiang. Qi Rang did not ask leave but sent his chief steward out to receive him.

sentences.zh: 英宗聞之不悅，賜書責讓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong heard of it he was displeased and bestowed a letter rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong was displeased when he heard of it and sent a letter of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 及嗣王，多不法，又待世子寡恩。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the princedom he committed many unlawful acts and also treated the heir apparent with little kindness.
translations.idiomatic: After he succeeded to the title he committed many unlawful acts and showed little kindness to his heir.

sentences.zh: 長史江萬程諫，被責辱，萬程以聞。

translations.literal: Chief steward Jiang Wancheng remonstrated, was rebuked and humiliated, and Jiang Wancheng reported it.
translations.idiomatic: His chief steward Jiang Wancheng remonstrated with him and was abused for it; Jiang reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝遣英國公張懋、太監王允中賫敕往諭，始上書謝罪。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Duke of Ying Zhang Mao and eunuch Wang Yunzhong bearing an edict to instruct him, whereupon he first submitted a memorial apologizing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Duke of Ying, Zhang Mao, and the eunuch Wang Yunzhong with an edict to admonish him, and only then did he submit a letter of apology.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Hongzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Hongzhi 8.

sentences.zh: 世子見滋母韓妃不為祁锳所禮，見滋悒悒先卒。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Jian Zi's mother, Consort Han, was not treated with courtesy by Qi Rang; Jian Zi, depressed, died first.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Jian Zi's mother, Consort Han, was ill-treated by Qi Rang; brooding over it, Jian Zi died before his father.

sentences.zh: 子康王祐枔嗣，正德二年薨。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Kang You Si, succeeded; in the second year of Zhengde he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son You Si, Prince Kang, succeeded him and died in Zhengde 2.

sentences.zh: 無子，從弟懿王祐檡嗣，十六年薨。

translations.literal: Having no son, his younger cousin Prince Yi You Lin succeeded; in the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, so his younger cousin You Lin, Prince Yi, succeeded; he died in the sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 子恭王厚烷嗣。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Gong Hou Wan, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hou Wan, Prince Gong, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 世宗幸承天，厚烷迎謁於新鄉，加祿三百石。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong visited Chengtian, Hou Wan met and paid homage at Xinxiang, and three hundred shi of stipend were added.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong traveled to Chengtian, Hou Wan met him at Xinxiang and was granted an additional three hundred shi of stipend.

sentences.zh: 疏奏母閻太妃貞孝事跡。

translations.literal: In a memorial he reported the chaste and filial conduct of his mother, Grand Consort Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the court on his mother Grand Consort Yan's chaste and filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 詔付史館。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it transmitted to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the account sent to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 其後帝修齋醮，諸王爭遣使進香，厚烷獨不遣。

translations.literal: Afterward, when the emperor performed fasting rites, the princes vied to send envoys offering incense; Hou Wan alone did not send any.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor held fasting rituals, the princes competed to send envoys with incense offerings, but Hou Wan alone sent none.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十七年七月上書，請帝修德講學，進《居敬》、《窮理》、《克己》、《存誠》四箴，《演連珠》十章，以神仙、土木為規諫。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-seventh year of Jiajing he submitted a memorial asking the emperor to cultivate virtue and pursue learning, presenting the four admonitions 《Dwelling in Reverence》, 《Exhausting Principle》, 《Overcoming the Self》, and 《Preserving Sincerity》, and ten chapters of 《Linked Pearls》, using immortals and construction works as admonitory examples.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Jiajing 27 he submitted a memorial urging the emperor to cultivate virtue and study, presenting his four admonitions 《Dwelling in Reverence》, 《Exhausting Principle》, 《Overcoming the Self》, and 《Preserving Sincerity》, together with ten chapters of 《Linked Pearls》, using the emperor's pursuit of immortals and building projects as his pointed warnings.

sentences.zh: 語切直。

translations.literal: The language was blunt and direct.
translations.idiomatic: His language was blunt and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下其使者於獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and imprisoned his envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and threw his envoy into prison.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「前宗室有謗訕者置不治，茲復效尤。

translations.literal: An edict said: Formerly, when members of the imperial clan slandered, they were left unpunished; now he again follows their bad example.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Before, when kinsmen of the imperial house slandered the throne, they were left unpunished; now he follows their bad example again.

sentences.zh: 王，今之西伯也，欲為為之。」

translations.literal: Prince, you are the Western Earl of today; do as you wish."
translations.idiomatic: Prince, you are the Duke of the West of our day — do as you please."

sentences.zh: 後二年而有祐橏之事，厚烷遂獲罪。

translations.literal: Two years later the affair of You Fu occurred, and Hou Wan was convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later came the affair of You Fu, and Hou Wan was condemned.

sentences.zh: 初，祁锳有子十人，世子見滋，次盟津王見濍，次東垣王見氵貢。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qi Rang had ten sons: the heir apparent Jian Zi; next the Prince of Mengjin, Jian Yin; next the Prince of Dongyuan, Jian Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qi Rang had ten sons: the heir Jian Zi; next Jian Yin, Prince of Mengjin; next Jian Bin, Prince of Dongyuan.

sentences.zh: 見濍母有寵於祁锳，規奪嫡，不得，竊世子金冊以去。

translations.literal: Jian Yin's mother was favored by Qi Rang; she plotted to seize the succession but failed, and stole the heir's golden patent and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yin's mother was favored by Qi Rang and plotted to displace the heir, but failed; she stole the heir's golden patent and fled.

sentences.zh: 祁锳索之急，因怨不復朝，所為益不法。

translations.literal: Qi Rang pressed the search urgently; because of resentment he no longer attended court, and his conduct grew more unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Rang pressed the search hard; nursing a grudge, Jian Yin stopped attending court, and his conduct grew ever more lawless.

sentences.zh: 祁锳言之憲宗，革為庶人。

translations.literal: Qi Rang reported it to Emperor Xianzong, and he was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Rang reported him to Emperor Xianzong, who stripped him to commoner rank.

sentences.zh: 及康王薨，無子，見濍子祐橏應及，以前罪廢，乃立東垣王子祐檡。

translations.literal: When Prince Kang died without a son, Jian Yin's son You Fu was next in line, but because of the earlier offense he was disqualified, and the son of the Prince of Dongyuan, You Lin, was established.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kang died childless, Jian Yin's son You Fu would have succeeded, but was passed over because of his father's crime; You Lin, son of the Prince of Dongyuan, was enthroned instead.

sentences.zh: 至是祐橏求復郡王爵，怨厚烷不為奏，乘帝怒，摭厚烷四十罪，以叛逆告。

translations.literal: At this time You Fu sought restoration of his commandery-prince rank, resented Hou Wan for not memorializing on his behalf, seized the emperor's anger, collected forty charges against Hou Wan, and reported rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: By then You Fu was petitioning to have his commandery-prince rank restored. Angry that Hou Wan would not speak for him, he seized on the emperor's wrath, compiled forty charges against Hou Wan, and accused him of treason.

sentences.zh: 詔駙馬中官即訊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered imperial sons-in-law and inner eunuchs to investigate on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered imperial sons-in-law and palace eunuchs to investigate immediately.

sentences.zh: 還報反無驗，治宮室名號擬乘輿則有之。

translations.literal: On their return they reported that rebellion was unverified, but that in his residence names and titles imitated the imperial carriage were found.
translations.idiomatic: They reported back that treason could not be substantiated, though his residence did use names and titles reserved for the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「厚烷訕朕躬，在國驕傲無禮，大不道。」

translations.literal: The emperor said in anger: Hou Wan has slandered my person; in his state he is arrogant and without propriety — a grave offense."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged: "Hou Wan has slandered my person; in his princedom he is arrogant and insolent — a capital offense."

sentences.zh: 削爵，錮之鳳陽。

translations.literal: His rank was stripped and he was confined at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His title was stripped and he was imprisoned at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年復王爵，增祿四百石。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing his princely rank was restored and four hundred shi of stipend were added.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1 his princely title was restored and his stipend increased by four hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 厚烷自少至老，布衣蔬食。

translations.literal: From youth to old age Hou Wan wore plain cloth and ate simple food.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age Hou Wan dressed in plain cloth and ate sparingly.

sentences.zh: 世子載堉篤學有至性，痛父非罪見系，築土室宮門外，席槁獨處者十九年。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Zai Yin was devoted to learning and of utmost filial nature; grieved that his father was imprisoned without crime, he built an earthen chamber outside the palace gate and lived alone on straw matting for nineteen years.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Zai Yin was a devoted scholar of deep filial feeling. Grieved that his father had been imprisoned without just cause, he built a hut of earth outside the palace gate and lived alone on a straw pallet for nineteen years.

sentences.zh: 厚烷還邸，始入宮。

translations.literal: When Hou Wan returned to his residence, he only then entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Hou Wan returned to his residence did Zai Yin enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十九年，厚烷薨。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Wanli, Hou Wan died.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Wan died in Wanli 19.

sentences.zh: 載堉曰：「鄭宗之序，盟津為長。

translations.literal: Zai Yin said: In the order of the house of Zheng, Mengjin is senior.
translations.idiomatic: Zai Yin said: "In the succession of the house of Zheng, the line of Mengjin is senior.

sentences.zh: 前王見濍，既錫謚復爵矣，爵宜歸盟津。」

translations.literal: The former prince Jian Yin has already been granted a posthumous title and had his rank restored; the title ought to return to Mengjin."
translations.idiomatic: The former Prince Jian Yin has already been given a posthumous title and had his rank restored; the title should pass to Mengjin."

sentences.zh: 後累疏懇辭。

translations.literal: Later he repeatedly submitted memorials earnestly declining.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted repeated memorials earnestly declining the succession.

sentences.zh: 禮臣言：「載堉雖深執讓節，然嗣鄭王已三世，無中更理，宜以載堉子翊錫嗣。」

translations.literal: The ritual officials said: Although Zai Yin deeply holds to the virtue of yielding, yet the succession to Prince of Zheng has already passed three generations without interruption in the middle; it is fitting that Zai Yin's son Yi Xi succeed."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials said: "Although Zai Yin is deeply committed to yielding, the line of the Prince of Zheng has already passed three generations without a break in the middle; Zai Yin's son Yi Xi ought to succeed."

sentences.zh: 載堉執奏如初，乃以祐橏之孫載璽嗣，而令載堉及翊錫以世子、世孫祿終其身，子孫仍封東垣王。

translations.literal: Zai Yin persisted in memorializing as before; thereupon You Fu's grandson Zai Xi succeeded, while Zai Yin and Yi Xi were granted heir and heir's son stipends for life, and their descendants were still enfeoffed as Princes of Dongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zai Yin persisted in his memorials as before. Thereupon You Fu's grandson Zai Xi was made heir, while Zai Yin and Yi Xi were granted heir and heir's-son stipends for life; their descendants were still enfeoffed as Princes of Dongyuan.

sentences.zh: 二十二年正月，載堉上疏，請宗室皆得儒服就試，毋論中外職，中式者視才品器使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-second year, Zai Yin submitted a memorial asking that all members of the imperial clan be allowed to wear scholar's dress and take examinations, regardless of inner or outer offices, and that those who passed be employed according to talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-second year, Zai Yin memorialized that all imperial clansmen be allowed to wear scholar's robes and sit for the examinations, without regard to inner or outer appointments, and that those who passed be employed according to talent and merit.

sentences.zh: 詔允行。

translations.literal: An edict approved and implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 明年又上歷算歲差之法，及所著《樂律書》，考辨詳確，識者稱之。

translations.literal: The next year he again submitted methods of calendrical calculation and precession of the equinoxes, and his work 《Treatise on Musical Temperament》; the examination and discrimination were detailed and exact, and those who understood praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he submitted his methods for calendrical calculation and the precession of the equinoxes, together with his 《Treatise on Musical Temperament》; his scholarship was meticulous, and experts praised it.

sentences.zh: 卒謚端清。

translations.literal: At death he was given the posthumous title Duan Qing.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously titled Duan Qing, Upright and Pure.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，載璽子翊鐘以罪賜死，國除。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen, Zai Xi's son Yi Zhong was sentenced to death by imperial gift for a crime, and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign, Zai Xi's son Yi Zhong was sentenced to death for his crimes, and the princedom was abolished.

sentences.zh: 廬江王載堙，簡王元孫也。

translations.literal: Prince of Lujiang, Zai Yan, was a great-grandson of Prince Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lujiang, Zai Yan, was a great-grandson of Prince Jian.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十七年二月，賊陷懷慶，載堙整冠服，端坐堂上。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, when bandits captured Huaiqing, Zai Yan straightened his cap and robes and sat upright in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Chongzhen 17, when rebels took Huaiqing, Zai Yan straightened his cap and robes and sat upright in the hall.

sentences.zh: 賊至，被執，欲屈之。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived he was seized; they wished to make him submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came he was seized and they tried to force him to submit.

sentences.zh: 歷聲曰：「吾天朝藩王，肯降汝逆賊耶！」

translations.literal: He cried out: I am a prince of the Celestial Dynasty — would I submit to you rebel bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: He shouted: "I am a prince of the Celestial Dynasty — would I bow to rebel bandits like you!"

sentences.zh: 詬罵不屈，遇害。

translations.literal: He reviled them and would not yield, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed them without yielding and was killed.

sentences.zh: 賊執其長子翊檭，擁之北行。

translations.literal: The bandits seized his eldest son Yi Lin and escorted him north.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized his eldest son Yi Lin and marched him north.

sentences.zh: 三月過定興，於旅店作絕命詞，遂不食死。

translations.literal: In the third month, passing Dingxing, he composed a death poem at an inn and then starved himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, passing through Dingxing, he wrote a final poem at an inn and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 越靖王瞻墉，仁宗第三子。

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Yue, Zhan Yong, was the third son of Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Yue, Zhan Yong, was Emperor Renzong's third son.

sentences.zh: 永樂二十二年封衢州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yongle he was enfeoffed at Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed at Quzhou in Yongle 22.

sentences.zh: 未之藩，宣宗賜以昌平莊田。

translations.literal: Before going to his fief, Emperor Xuanzong granted him estate fields at Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up his fief, Emperor Xuanzong granted him estate lands at Changping.

sentences.zh: 正統四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengtong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhengtong 4.

sentences.zh: 妃吳氏殉，謚貞惠。

translations.literal: Consort Wu followed him in death; she was posthumously titled Zhen Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu died with him and was posthumously titled Zhen Hui, Chaste and Kind.

sentences.zh: 無後。

translations.literal: He left no heir.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir.

sentences.zh: 蘄獻王瞻垠，仁宗第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi, Zhan Yin, was the fourth son of Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi, Zhan Yin, was Emperor Renzong's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 初封靜樂王。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Jingle.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Jingle.

sentences.zh: 永樂十九年薨，謚莊獻。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yongle he died; he was posthumously titled Zhuang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongle 19 and was posthumously titled Zhuang Xian.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，追加封謚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong acceded, his enfeoffment and posthumous title were added retroactively.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, his title and posthumous honors were conferred retroactively.

sentences.zh: 無後。

translations.literal: He left no heir.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir.

sentences.zh: 襄憲王瞻墡，仁宗第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Xiang, Zhan Fan, was the fifth son of Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Xiang, Zhan Fan, was Emperor Renzong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 永樂二十二年封。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yongle he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Yongle 22.

sentences.zh: 莊警有令譽。

translations.literal: Solemn and circumspect, he had an excellent reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn and dignified in bearing, he enjoyed an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年就藩長沙。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande he went to his fief at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 4 he took up his fief at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 正統元年徙襄陽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong he was moved to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 his fief was moved to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，諸王中，瞻墡最長且賢，眾望頗屬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was taken north on campaign, among the princes Zhan Fan was the eldest and most worthy, and popular expectation largely rested on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was captured on the northern campaign, Zhan Fan was the eldest and most worthy among the princes, and public hope largely turned to him.

sentences.zh: 太后命取襄國金符入宮，不果召。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered the golden tally of the state of Xiang brought into the palace, but he was not in the end summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered the golden tally of Xiang brought to the palace, but in the end he was never summoned.

sentences.zh: 瞻墡上書，請立皇長子，令郕王監國，募勇智士迎車駕。

translations.literal: Zhan Fan submitted a memorial asking that the eldest imperial son be established, that the Prince of Cheng supervise the state, and that brave and capable men be recruited to welcome back the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Fan memorialized the throne, urging that the eldest imperial son be named heir, that the Prince of Cheng supervise the realm, and that brave and capable men be enlisted to recover the emperor.

sentences.zh: 書至，景帝立數日矣。

translations.literal: When the letter arrived, the Jing Emperor had already been enthroned for several days.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the memorial reached court, the Jing Emperor had already reigned for several days.

sentences.zh: 英宗還京師，居南內，又上書景帝宜旦夕省膳問安，率群臣朔望見，無忘恭順。

translations.literal: The Ying Emperor returned to the capital, dwelt in the Southern Palace, and again submitted a memorial to the Jing Emperor that he should morning and evening inspect meals and inquire after his health, lead the ministers at the new and full moon to audience, and not forget deferential obedience.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital and settling in the Southern Palace, the Ying Emperor again wrote to the Jing Emperor, urging him to attend daily to his elder brother's meals and welfare, to lead the ministers in paying respects on the first and fifteenth of each month, and never to neglect his filial duty.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，石亨等誣于謙、王文有迎立外藩語，帝頗疑瞻墡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, Shi Heng and others falsely accused Yu Qian and Wang Wen of language inviting the establishment of an outer feudatory prince, and the emperor came to suspect Zhan Fan somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingzong regained the throne, Shi Heng and others falsely accused Yu Qian and Wang Wen of plotting to install an outer feudatory prince, and the emperor grew somewhat suspicious of Zhan Fan.

sentences.zh: 久之，從宮中得瞻墡所上二書，而襄國金符固在太后閣中。

translations.literal: After some time, from within the palace two memorials submitted by Zhan Fan were obtained, and the Xiang princedom's golden tally remained secure in the empress dowager's cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: In time two memorials Zhan Fan had submitted were recovered from within the palace, and the Xiang princedom's golden tally was still secure in the empress dowager's cabinet.

sentences.zh: 乃賜書召瞻墡，比二書於《金滕》。

translations.literal: Then an edict-letter was sent summoning Zhan Fan, comparing the two memorials to the "Golden Coffer" chapter.
translations.idiomatic: An edict-letter was then sent summoning Zhan Fan, likening the two memorials to the "Golden Coffer" chapter.

sentences.zh: 入朝，宴便殿，避席請曰：「臣過汴，汴父老遮道，言按察使王賢，以誣逮詔獄，願皇上加察。」

translations.literal: When he entered court, a banquet was held in the informal hall; he left his seat and requested: "When your subject passed through Bian, the elders of Bian blocked the road and spoke of Surveillance Commissioner Wang Xian, who had been imprisoned in the edict prison on a false charge; I beg Your Majesty to examine this closely."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court, a banquet was held in the informal hall. He rose from his seat and said, "When I passed through Bian, the local elders blocked the road and told me that Surveillance Commissioner Wang Xian had been thrown into the edict prison on a false charge. I beg Your Majesty to look into this."

sentences.zh: 帝立出槩，命為大理卿。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately released Gai and appointed him Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately released Gai and appointed him Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 詔設襄陽護衛，命有司為王營壽藏。

translations.literal: An edict established the Xiangyang Guard and ordered the officials to prepare the prince's tomb for him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict established the Xiangyang Guard and ordered officials to prepare the prince's tomb.

sentences.zh: 及歸，帝親送至午門外，握手泣別。

translations.literal: When he returned, the emperor personally escorted him outside the Meridian Gate, clasped his hand, and parted in tears.
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave to return, the emperor personally escorted him outside the Meridian Gate, clasped his hand, and wept as they parted.

sentences.zh: 瞻墡逡巡再拜，帝曰：「叔父欲何言？」

translations.literal: Zhan Fan hesitated and bowed twice; the emperor said, "What does Uncle wish to say?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Fan hesitated and bowed again. The emperor asked, "What did you wish to say, Uncle?"

sentences.zh: 頓首曰：「萬方望治如饑渴，願省刑薄斂。」

translations.literal: He kowtowed and said, "The myriad regions look to good governance as to thirst and hunger; I wish that punishments be reduced and levies lightened."
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed and said, "The realm longs for good government as for food and water. I hope Your Majesty will reduce punishments and lighten taxes."

sentences.zh: 帝拱謝曰：「敬受教。」

translations.literal: The emperor bowed with folded hands and replied, "I respectfully accept your instruction."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed with folded hands and replied, "I respectfully accept your counsel."

sentences.zh: 目送出端門乃還。

translations.literal: He watched until Zhan Fan passed through the Duan Gate before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He watched until Zhan Fan passed through the Duan Gate before returning.

sentences.zh: 四年復入朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he came to court again.

sentences.zh: 命百官朝王於邸，詔王詣昌平謁三陵。

translations.literal: He ordered all officials to attend upon the prince at his residence and commanded the prince to go to Changping to pay homage at the Three Tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all officials to attend the prince at his residence and commanded the prince to go to Changping to pay homage at the Three Tombs.

sentences.zh: 及辭歸，禮送加隆，且敕王歲時與諸子得出城遊獵，蓋異數也。

translations.literal: When he took leave to return, the courtesies of escort were augmented, and he and his sons were further permitted to leave the city each season to hunt—a mark of exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave to return, the courtesies of escort were heightened, and he and his sons were further permitted to leave the city each season to hunt—an exceptional privilege.

sentences.zh: 六年又召，以老辭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned again but declined on grounds of age.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he was summoned again but declined on account of old age.

sentences.zh: 歲時存問，禮遇之隆，諸藩所未有。

translations.literal: Seasonal inquiries were sent, and the courtesy shown him was grander than any princedom had ever received.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal inquiries were sent, and the honors shown him exceeded anything any princedom had known.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chenghua 14.

sentences.zh: 子定王祁鏞嗣，弘治元年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Ding Qi Yong succeeded; he died in the first year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was succeeded by his son, Prince Ding Qi Yong, who died in Hongzhi 1.

sentences.zh: 子簡王見淑嗣，三年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Jian Jian Shu succeeded; he died in the third year.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian Jian Shu succeeded him and died three years later.

sentences.zh: 子懷王祐材嗣。

translations.literal: Prince Huai You Cai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He was succeeded by Prince Huai You Cai.

sentences.zh: 好鷹犬，蓄善馬，往返南陽八百里，日猶未晡。

translations.literal: He loved hawks and hounds, kept excellent horses, and on an eight-hundred-li round trip to Nanyang still returned before late afternoon.
translations.idiomatic: Fond of falconry and hunting dogs, he kept fine horses and could cover the eight-hundred-li journey to Nanyang and back in a single day, arriving before mid-afternoon.

sentences.zh: 妃父井海誘使殺人。

translations.literal: His consort's father Jing Hai induced him to commit murder.
translations.idiomatic: His consort's father, Jing Hai, goaded him into ordering killings.

sentences.zh: 孝宗戒諭，戍海及其左右。

translations.literal: The Xiaozong Emperor admonished and instructed him; Hai and his followers were sent to frontier garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong reprimanded him and banished Hai and his associates to military service on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 祐材好道術，賜予無節，又嘗與興邸爭地，連逮七十余家，獄久不決。

translations.literal: You Cai loved Daoist arts, gave gifts without restraint, and had once contested land with the estate of Xing, involving more than seventy households in succession; the case long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: You Cai cultivated Daoist practices, lavished gifts without limit, and once disputed boundaries with the Prince of Xing's household, embroiling over seventy families in a lawsuit that dragged on for years.

sentences.zh: 大理卿汪綸兩解之，乃得已。

translations.literal: The chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review Wang Lun twice mediated and only then was the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister of justice Wang Lun mediated twice before the dispute could finally be settled.

sentences.zh: 十七年薨。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 弟康王祐櫍嗣，亦好道術。

translations.literal: His younger brother Prince Kang You Zhi succeeded; he too loved Daoist arts.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Prince Kang You Zhi succeeded him and was likewise devoted to Daoist practices.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十九年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing 29.

sentences.zh: 無子，從子莊王厚颎由陽山王嗣，定王曾孫也。

translations.literal: Having no son, the clansman's son Prince Zhuang Hou Feng succeeded from the title Prince of Yangshan; he was the great-grandson of Prince Ding.
translations.idiomatic: With no direct heir, the title passed from the Prince of Yangshan to his clansman's son Prince Zhuang Hou Feng, a great-grandson of Prince Ding.

sentences.zh: 時王邸災，先世蓄積一空。

translations.literal: At the time a fire struck the princely residence, and the accumulations of former generations were entirely lost.
translations.idiomatic: A fire had recently destroyed the princely residence, wiping out the family's accumulated wealth.

sentences.zh: 厚潁折節為恭儉，節祿以餉邊，進金助三殿工。

translations.literal: Hou Feng restrained himself to be respectful and frugal, economized his stipend to provision the frontier, and offered gold to assist work on the Three Halls.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Feng adopted a humble and austere manner, diverted part of his stipend to support frontier troops, and contributed gold toward rebuilding the Three Halls.

sentences.zh: 兩賜書幣。

translations.literal: Twice he was granted imperial letters and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rewarded him twice with written commendations and gifts.

sentences.zh: 事嫡母王太妃及生母潘太妃，以孝聞。

translations.literal: In serving his formal mother Grand Consort Wang and his birth mother Grand Consort Pan, he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for his devotion to his stepmother, Grand Consort Wang, and his birth mother, Grand Consort Pan.

sentences.zh: 潘卒，殯之東偏。

translations.literal: When Pan died, he laid out her coffin in the eastern wing.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Consort Pan died, he had her coffin placed in the eastern side-hall.

sentences.zh: 王太妃曰：「汝母有子，社稷是賴，無以我故避正寢。」

translations.literal: Grand Consort Wang said: "Your mother had a son upon whom the altars of state rely; do not on my account avoid the main bedchamber."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Consort Wang said: "Your mother bore the heir on whom the realm depends; do not refuse the main chamber on my account."

sentences.zh: 厚颎泣曰：「臣不敢以非禮加臣母。」

translations.literal: Hou Feng wept and said: "Your subject dares not treat my mother with impropriety."
translations.idiomatic: Hou Feng wept and replied: "I cannot treat my mother with any breach of ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 及葬，跣足扶櫬五十里。

translations.literal: When it came to the burial, he went barefoot and supported the bier for fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral he walked fifty li barefoot alongside the coffin.

sentences.zh: 士大夫過襄者，皆為韋布交。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials passing through Xiang all befriended him in coarse cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Every scholar-official who passed through Xiang became his friend, often in the plain dress of mourning.

sentences.zh: 四十五年薨。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-fifth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 子靖五載堯嗣，萬歷二十三年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Jing Zai Yao succeeded; in the twenty-third year of Wanli he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was succeeded by Prince Jing Zai Yao, who died in Wanli 23.

sentences.zh: 子翊銘嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yi Ming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ming succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年，張獻忠陷襄陽，遇害。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chongzhen, Zhang Xianzhong took Xiangyang, and he met with fatal harm.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 14, when Zhang Xianzhong captured Xiangyang, the prince was killed.

sentences.zh: 初，大學士楊嗣昌之視師也，以襄陽為軍府，增堞浚隍，貯五省餉金及弓刀火器。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Grand Secretary Yang Sichang inspected the armies, he made Xiangyang the military headquarters, added battlements and deepened the moat, and stored pay from five provinces plus bows, blades, and firearms.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Yang Sichang took command of the campaign, he made Xiangyang his headquarters, strengthened its walls and moat, and stockpiled funds from five provinces along with arms and gunpowder weapons.

sentences.zh: 是年二月，獻忠邀殺嗣昌使於道，奪其符驗，以數十騎紿入襄城。

translations.literal: That year in the second month, Xianzhong waylaid and killed Yang Sichang's messenger on the road, seized his credentials, and with several dozen horsemen deceived their way into Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month that year, Xianzhong ambushed and killed Yang Sichang's courier, seized his official credentials, and tricked his way into Xiangcheng with a few dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 夜半火作，遲明，賊大至。

translations.literal: At midnight fire broke out; toward dawn the rebels arrived in force.
translations.idiomatic: Fire erupted at midnight, and at dawn the rebel army poured in.

sentences.zh: 執翊銘南城樓，屬卮酒曰：「王無罪，王死，嗣昌得以死償王。」

translations.literal: Seizing Yi Ming on the south city tower, he passed a cup of wine and said: "The prince is without guilt; when the prince dies, Sichang may repay the prince with his own death."
translations.idiomatic: They seized Yi Ming on the south gate tower; Xianzhong offered him a cup of wine and said: "You are innocent, but when you die, Sichang will owe you a life in return."

sentences.zh: 遂殺王及貴陽王常法，火城樓，焚其屍。

translations.literal: Thereupon they killed the prince and Prince of Guiyang Chang Fa, set fire to the city tower, and burned their corpses.
translations.idiomatic: They then killed the prince and Prince of Guiyang Chang Fa, torched the gate tower, and burned the bodies.

sentences.zh: 賊去，僅拾顱骨數寸，妃妾輩死者四十三人。

translations.literal: When the rebels departed, only a few inches of skull could be gathered; among consorts and concubines forty-three died.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels withdrew, only a few inches of skull remained to be recovered; forty-three of his consorts and concubines were slain.

sentences.zh: 福清王常澄、進賢王常淦走免。

translations.literal: Prince of Fuqing Chang Cheng and Prince of Jinxian Chang Gan fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Fuqing Chang Cheng and Prince of Jinxian Chang Gan managed to flee.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝震悼，命所司備喪禮，謚曰忠王。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor was shaken with grief and ordered the offices to prepare funeral rites; the posthumous title was Loyal Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stricken with grief on hearing the news and ordered a full state funeral; the prince was posthumously titled Loyal.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌朝惠王於荊州，謁者謝之曰：「先生惠顧寡人，願先之襄陽。」

translations.literal: Sichang had an audience with Prince of Hui at Jingzhou; the usher declined on his behalf, saying: "My lord has honored us with a visit; please go first to Xiangyang."
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Sichang called on Prince of Hui at Jingzhou, an attendant brushed him off: "His Highness graciously receives you, but he asks that you visit Xiangyang first."

sentences.zh: 謂襄城之破，罪在嗣昌也。

translations.literal: He meant that the fall of Xiangcheng was Sichang's fault.
translations.idiomatic: The rebuff implied that the blame for Xiangcheng's fall lay with Sichang.

sentences.zh: 十七年以常澄嗣襄王，寄居九江，後徙汀州，不知所終。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Chang Cheng succeeded as Prince of Xiang, resided at Jiujiang, later moved to Tingzhou; his final end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Chang Cheng inherited the title of Prince of Xiang, took refuge at Jiujiang, and later relocated to Tingzhou; his ultimate fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 棗陽王祐楒，憲王曾孫也，材武善文章，博涉星歷醫卜之書。

translations.literal: Prince of Zaoyang You Si, a great-grandson of Prince Xian, was talented in martial arts and skilled in literary composition, broadly versed in works on astrology, medicine, and divination.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zaoyang You Si, a great-grandson of Prince Xian, combined martial prowess with literary talent and was widely read in astronomy, medicine, and divination.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初上書，請考興獻帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he submitted a memorial asking that the Emperor Xingxian be enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he memorialized the throne, requesting proper enshrinement for Emperor Xingxian.

sentences.zh: 世宗以其議發自宗人，足厭服群心，褒之。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor, because this proposal issued from a clansman of the imperial house, considered it sufficient to satisfy and compel the hearts of the multitude, and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong Emperor praised him, holding that a proposal from within the imperial clan itself would better satisfy court and public opinion.

sentences.zh: 更請除宗人祿，使以四民業自為生，賢者用射策應科第。

translations.literal: He further asked that stipends to imperial clansmen be abolished, that they support themselves by the occupations of the four classes of people, and that the worthy among them enter officialdom through archery-and-writing examinations for the civil ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He further urged abolishing princely stipends so that clansmen would earn their livelihood as ordinary farmers, artisans, merchants, and scholars, with the ablest competing through the regular examination system.

sentences.zh: 寢不行。

translations.literal: The proposal was shelved and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was shelved and never enacted.

sentences.zh: 時襄王祐櫍病廢不事事，承奉邵亨挾權自恣，至捶死鎮寧王舅。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Xiang You Zhi was ill and incapacitated and did not attend to affairs; the attendant Shao Heng wielded power as he pleased, even beating to death the maternal uncle of the Prince of Zhenning.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Xiang You Zhi was bedridden and inactive; his chief attendant Shao Heng abused his authority, going so far as to beat the Prince of Zhenning's uncle to death.

sentences.zh: 祐楒誘致之，抉其目。

translations.literal: You Si lured him in and gouged out his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: You Si lured Shao Heng in and had his eyes put out.

sentences.zh: 帝遣大理少卿袁宗儒偕中官、錦衣往訊。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Zongru together with eunuchs and the Embroidered Uniform Guard to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister Yuan Zongru of the Court of Judicial Review, along with eunuchs and Imperial Guard officers, to conduct an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 亨論死，祐楒坐奪爵。

translations.literal: Heng was sentenced to death; You Si was punished by deprivation of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Heng was condemned to death, while You Si was stripped of his princely rank.

sentences.zh: 帝幸承天，念祐楒前疏，復之。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Chengtian, recalling You Si's earlier memorial, he restored his title.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Chengtian, the emperor remembered You Si's earlier petition and restored his rank.

sentences.zh: 荊憲王瞻堈，仁宗第六子。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Jing, Zhan Ju, was the sixth son of Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Jing, Zhan Ju, was Emperor Renzong's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 永樂二十二年封。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yongle he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Yongle 22.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年就藩建昌。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande he went to his fief at Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 4 he took up his fief at Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 宮中有巨蛇，蜿蜒自梁垂地，或憑王座。

translations.literal: In the palace was a huge serpent that wound down from the rafters to the ground, sometimes coiling upon the princely seat.
translations.idiomatic: A gigantic serpent dwelt in the palace, slithering down from the beams to the floor and sometimes curling upon the prince's throne.

sentences.zh: 瞻堈大懼，請徙。

translations.literal: Zhan Ju was greatly frightened and requested relocation.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhan Ju petitioned to be moved elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 正統十年徙蘄州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengtong he was moved to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 10 his fief was transferred to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年上書請朝上皇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai he submitted a memorial requesting an audience with the retired emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 2 he memorialized the throne, asking permission to pay homage to the retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died four years later.

sentences.zh: 子靖王祁鎬嗣，天順五年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Jing Qi Hao succeeded; he died in the fifth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He was succeeded by Prince Jing Qi Hao, who died in Tianshun 5.

sentences.zh: 子見潚嗣。

translations.literal: Jian Si succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Si succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 靖王三子，長見潚，次都王梁見溥、樊山王見澋。

translations.literal: The Jing prince had three sons: the eldest, Jian Si; next, Prince Du of Liang, Jian Pu, and the Fanshan prince, Jian Hong.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing prince had three sons: the eldest, Jian Si; next, Prince Du of Liang, Jian Pu; and the Fanshan prince, Jian Hong.

sentences.zh: 見潚與見溥同母，怨母之匿見溥也，錮母，奪其衣食，竟死，出柩於竇。

translations.literal: Jian Si and Jian Pu shared the same mother; resenting that she had concealed Jian Pu, he confined his mother, deprived her of food and clothing, and she ultimately died; her coffin was placed in a side room.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Si and Jian Pu had the same mother. Resenting that she had hidden Jian Pu, he confined her, stripped her of food and clothing, and she died; her coffin was placed in a side room.

sentences.zh: 召見溥入後園，箠殺之。

translations.literal: He summoned Jian Pu into the rear garden and beat him to death with a cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Jian Pu into the rear garden and beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 紿其妃何氏入宮，逼淫之。

translations.literal: He deceived Princess He into entering the palace and forced himself on her.
translations.idiomatic: He deceived Princess He into entering the palace and raped her.

sentences.zh: 從弟都昌王見潭妻茆氏美，求通焉。

translations.literal: His cousin the Prince of Duchang, Jian Tan, had a beautiful wife, the Lady Mao; he sought relations with her.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Prince of Duchang Jian Tan had a beautiful wife, Lady Mao; he sought an affair with her.

sentences.zh: 見潭母馬氏防之嚴，見潚髡馬氏鞭之，囊土壓見潭死，械系茆妃入宮。

translations.literal: Jian Tan's mother Lady Ma guarded her strictly; Jian Si shaved Lady Ma's head and flogged her, suffocated Jian Tan under sacks of earth, and shackled Princess Mao and brought her into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Tan's mother Lady Ma guarded her strictly. Jian Si shaved Lady Ma's head and flogged her, suffocated Jian Tan under sacks of earth, and shackled Princess Mao and brought her into the palace.

sentences.zh: 嘗集惡少年，輕騎徽服，涉漢水，掠人妻女。

translations.literal: He would gather wicked youths, ride lightly in plain dress, cross the Han River, and abduct men's wives and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: He would gather ruffians, ride lightly in plain dress, cross the Han River, and abduct women.

sentences.zh: 見澋懼其及也，密聞於孝宗，召至京。

translations.literal: Jian Hong feared he would reach him and secretly reported to Emperor Xiaozong; Jian Si was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would be next, Jian Hong secretly reported to Emperor Xiaozong, and Jian Si was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝御文華門，命廷臣會鞫。

translations.literal: The emperor presided at the Wenhua Gate and ordered court ministers to try the case jointly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor presided at the Wenhua Gate and ordered court ministers to try the case together.

sentences.zh: 見潚引伏，廢為庶人，錮西內。

translations.literal: Jian Si confessed; he was degraded to commoner status and confined in the Western Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Si confessed. He was stripped of rank, reduced to commoner status, and confined in the Western Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 居二年，見潚從西內摭奏見澋罪，誣其與楚府永安王謀不軌。

translations.literal: After two years, Jian Si from the Western Inner Palace gathered charges against Jian Hong, falsely accusing him of plotting treason with the Prince of Yong'an of the Chu princedom.
translations.idiomatic: After two years, Jian Si from the Western Inner Palace fabricated charges against Jian Hong, falsely accusing him of plotting treason with the Prince of Yong'an of the Chu princedom.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使往按問，不實。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys to investigate; it was not true.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to investigate; the accusation proved false.

sentences.zh: 見澋更奏見潚嘗私造弓弩，與子祐柄有異謀。

translations.literal: Jian Hong in turn memorialized that Jian Si had secretly made bows and crossbows and that he and his son You Bing harbored treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Hong then memorialized that Jian Si had secretly made bows and crossbows and that he and his son You Bing harbored treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 驗之實，賜見潚死，廢祐衲，而以見溥子祐橺嗣為荊王。

translations.literal: When this was verified as true, Jian Si was granted death by imperial command, You Na was degraded, and Jian Pu's son You Qiao succeeded as Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When this was verified, Jian Si was ordered to die, You Na was degraded, and Jian Pu's son You Qiao succeeded as Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 時弘治七年也。

translations.literal: This was in the seventh year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: This was in Hongzhi 7.

sentences.zh: 十七年薨，謚曰和。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died; his posthumous title was He.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year and was posthumously titled He.

sentences.zh: 子端王厚烇嗣。

translations.literal: Prince Duan Hou Quan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duan Hou Quan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 性謙和，銳意典籍。

translations.literal: By nature modest and gentle, he devoted himself zealously to the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and unassuming by nature, he devoted himself to classical learning.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中病，辭祿。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he fell ill and declined his stipend.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing era he fell ill and asked to surrender his stipend.

sentences.zh: 不允，令富順王厚焜攝朝謁。

translations.literal: This was not granted; he was ordered that Prince of Fushun Hou Kun act in his stead for court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused and instead appointed Prince of Fushun Hou Kun to represent him at official audiences.

sentences.zh: 厚焜，和王第二子，與弟永新王厚熿以能詩善畫名。

translations.literal: Hou Kun, the second son of the Prince of He, and his younger brother Prince of Yongxin Hou Huang were famed for skill in poetry and painting.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Kun, second son of the Prince of He, and his younger brother Prince of Yongxin Hou Huang were celebrated poets and painters.

sentences.zh: 厚烇子永定王載墭長，厚焜即謝攝事，人尤以為賢。

translations.literal: Hou Quan's son Prince of Yongding Zai Pei was the eldest; Hou Kun thereupon declined the acting duties, and people especially regarded this as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Quan's eldest son, Prince of Yongding Zai Pei, came of age, Hou Kun voluntarily relinquished his proxy duties, a move widely admired as exemplary.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十二年，厚烇薨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Jiajing Hou Quan died.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Quan died in Jiajing 32.

sentences.zh: 載墭己前卒，其子恭王翊鉅嗣。

translations.literal: Zai Pei had already died earlier; his son Prince Gong Yi Ju succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zai Pei had predeceased his father, so his son Prince Gong Yi Ju inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 荊自靖王諸子交惡，失令譽。

translations.literal: From Prince Jing's sons onward in Jing, mutual enmity prevailed among them, and they lost their fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the sons of Prince Jing, the Jing princes feuded among themselves and forfeited their family's good name.

sentences.zh: 及厚烇兄弟感先世家難，以禮讓訓飭宗人。

translations.literal: When it came to Hou Quan and his brothers, mindful of the family's past tribulations, they instructed the clansmen in ritual and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Quan and his brothers, mindful of the family's earlier disgrace, taught their kinsmen courtesy and restraint.

sentences.zh: 見澋曾孫載埁尤折節恭謹，以文行稱。

translations.literal: Jian Huang's great-great-grandson Zai Cheng especially restrained himself in reverent prudence and was famed for literary conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zai Cheng, a great-great-grandson of Jian Huang, was especially humble and dutiful, and won renown for scholarship and moral character.

sentences.zh: 郡王女例請祿於朝，載埁四女皆妻士人，不請封。

translations.literal: By custom daughters of commandery princes request stipends at court; Zai Cheng's four daughters all married common scholars and did not request enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Daughters of commandery princes customarily petitioned the court for stipends, but all four of Zai Cheng's daughters married common scholars without seeking titles or income.

sentences.zh: 嘗上《應詔》、《正禮》二疏。

translations.literal: He once submitted two memorials, 《Response to the Imperial Edict》 and 《Correcting Ritual》.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted two memorials, 《In Reply to the Imperial Edict》 and 《On Correct Ritual Practice》.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court never replied.

sentences.zh: 讀《易》窮理，著《大隱山人集》。

translations.literal: Reading the 《Changes》, he pursued principle to its depths and compiled the 《Collected Works of the Great Recluse》.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply versed in the 《Book of Changes》, he wrote the 《Collected Works of the Great Recluse》.

sentences.zh: 子翊𬫌、翊、翊皆工詩，兄弟嘗共處一樓，號花萼社。

translations.literal: His sons Yi Xi, Yi, and Yi were all skilled at poetry; the brothers once dwelt together in one tower, calling themselves the Flower-and-Calyx Society.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yi Xi and his brothers, all accomplished poets, once shared a single tower and styled themselves the Flower-and-Calyx Society.

sentences.zh: 翊鉅表載埁賢以訓諸子。

translations.literal: Yi Ju memorialized Zai Cheng's worth to instruct the sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ju held up Zai Cheng as a model of virtue for his sons to emulate.

sentences.zh: 諸子不率教，世子常泠尤殘恣。

translations.literal: The sons did not follow instruction; the heir Chang Ling was especially cruel and willful.
translations.idiomatic: The sons refused to heed his teaching, and the heir Chang Ling was especially brutal and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 翊鉅言於朝，革為庶人。

translations.literal: Yi Ju reported to the court, and he was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ju petitioned the throne, and Chang Ling was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年，翊鉅薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing Yi Ju died.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ju died in Longqing 4.

sentences.zh: 次子常𣵧嗣，萬歷四年薨。

translations.literal: The second son Chang Ni succeeded; he died in the fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Chang Ni succeeded and died in Wanli 4.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟康王常由安城王嗣，萬歷二十五年薨。

translations.literal: Having no son, his younger brother Prince Kang Chang You, Prince of Ancheng, succeeded; he died in the twenty-fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, his younger brother Prince Kang Chang You, Prince of Ancheng, succeeded and died in Wanli 25.

sentences.zh: 子定王由樊嗣，天啟二年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Ding You Fan succeeded; he died in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Ding You Fan succeeded and died in Tianqi 2.

sentences.zh: 子慈嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ci succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ci succeeded.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，流賊革裏眼、左金王詭降於楚帥。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen era the bandits Ge Liyan and Zuo Jinwang falsely surrendered to the commander in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen era the bandits Ge Liyan and Zuo Jinwang feigned surrender to the Huguang commander.

sentences.zh: 慈欲與為好，召宴，盛陳女樂。

translations.literal: Ci wished to cultivate friendship with them and summoned them to a banquet, lavishly displaying female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Ci sought friendship with them, summoned them to a banquet, and lavishly displayed female musicians.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，張獻忠陷蘄州，慈先一月薨。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year Zhang Xianzhong captured Qizhou; Ci had died the month before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 16 Zhang Xianzhong captured Qizhou; Ci had died the month before.

sentences.zh: 賊圍王宮，盡掠其所見妓樂去。

translations.literal: The bandits besieged the princely palace and carried off all the musicians and courtesans they found.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels besieged the princely palace and carried off all the musicians and courtesans they found.

sentences.zh: 淮靖王蟾墺，仁宗第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Huai, Zhan Ao, was the seventh son of Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Huai, Zhan Ao, was Emperor Renzong's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 永樂二十二年封。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yongle he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Yongle 22.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年就藩韶州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande he went to his fief at Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 4 he took up his fief at Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位之十月，以韶多瘴癘，正統元年徙饒州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month after the Ying Emperor's accession, because Shaozhou had much malarial pestilence, in the first year of Zhengtong he was moved to Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month after the Ying Emperor's accession, because Shaozhou was rife with malaria, his fief was moved to Raozhou in Zhengtong 1.

sentences.zh: 正統十一年薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhengtong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhengtong 11.

sentences.zh: 子康王祁銓嗣，弘治十五年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Kang Qi Quan succeeded; he died in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was succeeded by Prince Kang Qi Quan, who died in Hongzhi 15.

sentences.zh: 世子見濂早卒，無子，從子定王祐啟嗣。

translations.literal: The heir Jian Lian died early and left no son; the clansman's son Prince Ding You Qi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Jian Lian died young without issue, and the title passed to his clansman's son Prince Ding You Qi.

sentences.zh: 遊戲無度，左右倚勢暴橫，境內苦之。

translations.literal: He played without restraint; his attendants relied on power and were violent and overbearing, and the realm within his fief suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged in endless amusements while his retainers abused their authority and terrorized the countryside.

sentences.zh: 長史莊典以輔導失職自免。

translations.literal: The chief administrator Zhuang Dian resigned on the grounds of failure in guidance and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrator Zhuang Dian resigned, citing his failure as tutor and adviser.

sentences.zh: 詔不許。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit this.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused to accept his resignation.

sentences.zh: 推官汪文盛數持王府事。

translations.literal: The investigating magistrate Wang Wensheng repeatedly took charge of princely-house affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating magistrate Wang Wensheng repeatedly intervened in the affairs of the princely household.

sentences.zh: 有顧嵩者病狂，持刀斧入王門，官校執詰之，謬言出汪指使。

translations.literal: One Gu Song was deranged; wielding knife and axe he entered the princely gate, and when official guards seized and questioned him, he falsely said he had been instigated by Wang.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Gu Song, deranged, entered the palace gates armed with a knife and axe; when guards seized and questioned him, he falsely claimed Wang Wensheng had sent him.

sentences.zh: 典白之守臣。

translations.literal: Dian reported this to the provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Dian reported the matter to the provincial authorities.

sentences.zh: 鎮守太監黎安嘗以事至饒，從騎入端禮門，被撻，銜祐棨甚。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuch Li An had once come to Raozhou on business; his mounted escort entered the Duanli Gate and was flogged, and he bore a deep grudge against You Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison eunuch Li An had once visited Raozhou on official business; when his mounted escort entered the Duanli Gate they were beaten, and he nursed a deep grudge against You Qi.

sentences.zh: 先是，祐棨有名琴曰「天風環佩」，寧王宸濠求之，不得。

translations.literal: Earlier, You Qi had a famous zither called "Heavenly Wind and Ringing Jade"; the Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao sought it but did not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: You Qi owned a celebrated zither called "Heavenly Wind and Ringing Jade," which Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao had sought in vain.

sentences.zh: 又求濱湖地，不與。

translations.literal: He also sought lakeside land and was not given it.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao also demanded lakeside land and was refused.

sentences.zh: 至是嗾安奏祐棨過失及文盛被誣事。

translations.literal: At this point he instigated An to memorialize You Qi's faults and the matter of Wen Sheng's false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture he prompted Li An to denounce You Qi's misconduct and the frame-up of Wang Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 詔下撫按訊。

translations.literal: An edict was issued ordering the provincial governor and censor to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the provincial governor and censor to conduct an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 安與宸濠謀，不待報，遽系典及府中官校鞫之。

translations.literal: An and Chenhao plotted; without awaiting a reply, they hastily seized Dian and the princely-house guards and interrogated them.
translations.idiomatic: Li An and Chenhao conspired to arrest Zhuang Dian and the princely guards and interrogate them before any official report came back.

sentences.zh: 典辭倨，宸濠箠之，斃獄中，他所連坐甚眾。

translations.literal: Dian's words were haughty; Chenhao beat him with a whip, and he died in prison; those implicated elsewhere were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Dian answered defiantly; Chenhao had him flogged to death in prison, and many others were implicated as well.

sentences.zh: 於是祐棨奏安挾仇殺典庇嵩。

translations.literal: Thereupon You Qi memorialized that An, bearing a private grudge, had killed Dian and shielded Song.
translations.idiomatic: You Qi then petitioned the throne, charging that Li An had murdered Zhuang Dian out of personal spite while protecting Gu Song.

sentences.zh: 帝遣都御史金獻民、太監張欽往按治。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Censor-in-Chief Jin Xianmin and the eunuch Zhang Qin to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Censor-in-Chief Jin Xianmin and the eunuch Zhang Qin to conduct a full investigation.

sentences.zh: 祐棨畏宸濠，不能自明。

translations.literal: You Qi feared Chenhao and could not clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: You Qi was afraid of Chenhao and could not vindicate himself.

sentences.zh: 欽等復言祐棨信奸徒為暴，請嚴戒之。

translations.literal: Qin and the others again said that You Qi trusted wicked men to commit violence and asked that he be strictly warned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qin and his party again reported that You Qi had trusted ruffians to commit outrages and petitioned that he be sternly admonished.

sentences.zh: 軍校坐戍者二十余人，典冤竟不白。

translations.literal: More than twenty military officers were punished with frontier service; Dian's injustice was never cleared in the end.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty officers and guards were sentenced to frontier duty, and Zhuang Dian's wrongful conviction was never overturned.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，祐棨薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing You Qi died.
translations.idiomatic: You Qi died in Jiajing 3.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟莊王祐楑嗣，十六年薨。

translations.literal: Having no son, his younger brother Prince Zhuang You Juan succeeded; he died in the sixteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, his younger brother Prince Zhuang You Juan succeeded and died in year 16.

sentences.zh: 子憲王厚燾嗣，四十二年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Xian Hou Tao succeeded; he died in the forty-second year.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Xian Hou Tao succeeded and died in year 42.

sentences.zh: 子恭王載坮嗣，萬歷五年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Gong Zai Tai succeeded; he died in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Gong Zai Tai succeeded and died in Wanli 5.

sentences.zh: 弟順王載堅嗣，二十三年薨。

translations.literal: His younger brother Prince Shun Zai Jian succeeded; he died in the twenty-third year.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Prince Shun Zai Jian succeeded and died in year 23.

sentences.zh: 子翊𨨣嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yi Ju succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi Ju succeeded.

sentences.zh: 翊𨨣之未王也，與妓王愛狎，冒妾額入宮，且令撫庶子常洪為子，陳妃與世子常清俱失愛，潛謀易嫡。

translations.literal: Before Yi Ju became prince, he was intimate with the courtesan Wang Ai; he falsely entered her name as a concubine in the household register and brought her into the palace, and also had her raise the secondary son Chang Hong as his own; Consort Chen and the heir Chang Qing both lost favor and secretly plotted to change the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yi Ju became prince, he was intimate with the courtesan Wang Ai. He falsely entered her name as a concubine in the household register and brought her into the palace, and had her raise the secondary son Chang Hong as his own. Consort Chen and the heir Chang Qing both lost favor and secretly plotted to change the succession.

sentences.zh: 御史陳王道以理諭王，出之外舍。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Wangdao reasoned with the prince and had Wang Ai removed to an outside lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Wangdao reasoned with the prince and had Wang Ai removed to an outside lodge.

sentences.zh: 常洪遂與宗人翊銂等謀，夜入王宮，盜冊寶、資貨以出。

translations.literal: Chang Hong then conspired with clansman Yi Xin and others; by night they entered the princely palace and stole the registers, seals, and valuables before making off.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Hong then conspired with clansman Yi Xin and others. By night they entered the princely palace and stole the registers, seals, and valuables before fleeing.

sentences.zh: 守臣上其事，王愛論死，勒常洪自盡，翊銂等削屬籍永錮，奪翊𨨣四歲祿。

translations.literal: The provincial commander reported the matter; Wang Ai was sentenced to death, Chang Hong was compelled to take his own life, Yi Xin and the others were struck from the clansman's register and permanently confined, and four years of Yi Ju's stipend were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial commander reported the matter. Wang Ai was sentenced to death, Chang Hong was compelled to take his own life, Yi Xin and the others were struck from the clansman's register and permanently confined, and four years of Yi Ju's stipend were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 久之，薨。

translations.literal: After some time he died.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he died.

sentences.zh: 子常清嗣，國亡，不知所終。

translations.literal: His son Chang Qing succeeded; when the state fell, his final fate was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang Qing succeeded. When the dynasty fell, his final fate was unknown.

sentences.zh: 滕懷王瞻塏，仁宗第八子。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Teng, Zhan Kai, was the eighth son of Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Teng, Zhan Kai, was Emperor Renzong's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 永樂二十二年封雲南，未之國，洪熙元年薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yongle he was enfeoffed at Yunnan but did not go to his fief; he died in the first year of Hongxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 22 he was enfeoffed at Yunnan but never went to his fief. He died in Hongxi 1.

sentences.zh: 無後。

translations.literal: He left no descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He left no descendants.

sentences.zh: 梁莊王瞻垍，仁宗第九子。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang of Liang, Zhan Ji, was the ninth son of Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuang of Liang, Zhan Ji, was Emperor Renzong's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 永樂二十二年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in Yongle 22.
translations.idiomatic: He received his princely title in the twenty-second year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，詔鄭、越、襄、荊、淮五王歲給鈔五萬貫，惟梁倍之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande, an edict granted the five princes of Zheng, Yue, Xiang, Jing, and Huai fifty thousand strings of paper money each year; only Liang received double.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuande, the throne ordered that the Princes of Zheng, Yue, Xiang, Jing, and Huai each receive fifty thousand strings of paper money annually, but the Prince of Liang was allotted twice that amount.

sentences.zh: 四年就藩安陸，故郢邸也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went to his fief at Anlu, the former residence of the Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he took up his fief at Anlu, which had been the seat of the Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 襄王瞻墡自長沙徙襄陽，道安陸，與瞻垍留連不忍去。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiang, Zhan Fan, moved from Changsha to Xiangyang; passing through Anlu, he lingered with Zhan Ji and could not bear to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xiang, Zhan Fan, relocated from Changsha to Xiangyang, he traveled by way of Anlu and lingered with Zhan Ji, unwilling to part.

sentences.zh: 瀕別，瞻垍慟曰：「兄弟不復更相見，奈何！」

translations.literal: On the verge of parting, Zhan Ji grieved and said: "Brothers will not meet again -- what is to be done!"
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to separate, Zhan Ji wept and said, "We brothers shall never see each other again -- what can be done!"

sentences.zh: 左右皆泣下。

translations.literal: Those on either side all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Those around them all burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 正統元年言府卑濕，乞更爽塏地。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong 1 he said the princely residence was low and damp and begged for drier, higher ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengtong he reported that his residence was low-lying and damp and asked to be moved to drier, more open ground.

sentences.zh: 帝詔郢中歲歉，俟有秋理之。

translations.literal: The emperor decreed that Ying had had poor harvests that year and that it should be dealt with when autumn came.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that the Ying region had suffered poor harvests that year and that the matter should wait until a better season.

sentences.zh: 竟不果。

translations.literal: In the end it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the end nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 六年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 無子，封除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son, and the princely line was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 梁故得郢田宅園湖，後皆賜襄王。

translations.literal: Liang had formerly held the fields, houses, gardens, and lakes of Ying; afterward these were all granted to the Prince of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang had originally held the fields, estates, gardens, and lakes of the Ying fief, but these were later all granted to the Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 及睿宗封安陸，盡得郢、梁邸田，供二王祠祀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong was enfeoffed at Anlu, he obtained all the fields of the Ying and Liang residences to supply sacrifices for the two princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong was granted Anlu, he received all the lands of the Ying and Liang establishments to support the ancestral rites of the two princes.

sentences.zh: 衛恭王瞻埏，仁宗第十子。

translations.literal: Prince Gong of Wei, Zhan Yan, was the tenth son of Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong of Wei, Zhan Yan, was Emperor Renzong's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 永樂二十二年封懷慶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yongle he was enfeoffed at Huaiqing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 22 he was enfeoffed at Huaiqing.

sentences.zh: 幼善病，宣宗撫愛之，未就藩。

translations.literal: From youth he was prone to illness; Emperor Xuanzong cherished him, and he did not go to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was prone to illness. Emperor Xuanzong cherished him, and he never went to his fief.

sentences.zh: 歲時謁陵，皆命攝祀。

translations.literal: At the seasonal tomb observances he was always ordered to officiate in proxy.
translations.idiomatic: At the seasonal tomb observances he was always ordered to officiate in proxy.

sentences.zh: 孝謹好學，以賢聞。

translations.literal: Filial, careful, and fond of learning, he was known for worthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Filial, careful, and fond of learning, he was known for his virtue.

sentences.zh: 正統三年薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhengtong 3.

sentences.zh: 妃楊氏殉，賜謚貞烈。

translations.literal: Consort Yang followed him in death; she was granted the posthumous title Zhenlie.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang followed him in death and was granted the posthumous title Zhenlie.

sentences.zh: 無子，封除。

translations.literal: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.

sentences.zh: 英宗九子。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong had nine sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong had nine sons.

sentences.zh: 周太后生憲宗、崇王見澤。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhou bore Emperor Xianzong and Prince Chong Jian Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhou bore Emperor Xianzong and Prince Chong Jian Ze.

sentences.zh: 萬宸妃生德王見潾及皇子見湜、吉王見浚、忻王見治。

translations.literal: Consort Wan Chen bore Prince De Jian Lin as well as the imperial sons Jian Shi, Prince Ji Jian Jun, and Prince Xin Jian Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wan Chen bore Prince De Jian Lin as well as the imperial sons Jian Shi, Prince Ji Jian Jun, and Prince Xin Jian Zhi.

sentences.zh: 王惠妃生許王見淳。

translations.literal: Consort Wang Hui bore Prince Xu Jian Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang Hui bore Prince Xu Jian Chun.

sentences.zh: 高淑妃生秀王見澍。

translations.literal: Consort Gao Shu bore Prince Xiu Jian Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Gao Shu bore Prince Xiu Jian Shu.

sentences.zh: 韋德妃生徽王見沛。

translations.literal: Consort Wei De bore Prince Hui Jian Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wei De bore Prince Hui Jian Pei.

sentences.zh: 德莊王見潾，英宗第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang of De, Jian Lin, was the second son of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuang of De, Jian Lin, was Emperor Yingzong's second son.

sentences.zh: 初名見清。

translations.literal: His original name was Jian Qing.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Jian Qing.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年封榮王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai he was enfeoffed as Prince of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 3 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Rong.

sentences.zh: 天順元年三月復東宮，同日封德、秀、崇、吉四王，歲祿各萬石。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Tianshun the Eastern Palace was restored; on the same day the four princes De, Xiu, Chong, and Ji were enfeoffed, each with an annual stipend of ten thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianshun 1 the Eastern Palace was restored; on the same day the four princes De, Xiu, Chong, and Ji were enfeoffed, each with an annual stipend of ten thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 初國德州，改濟南。

translations.literal: Initially his state was at Dezhou; it was changed to Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Initially his fief was at Dezhou; it was later changed to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 成化三年就藩。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chenghua he went to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 3 he went to his fief.

sentences.zh: 請得齊、漢二庶人所遺東昌、充州閑田及白雲、景陽、廣平三湖地。

translations.literal: He requested to obtain the idle fields of Dongchang and Yanzhou left by the two deposed commoners of Qi and Han, as well as the lands of the three lakes Baiyun, Jingyang, and Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He requested the idle fields of Dongchang and Yanzhou left by the two deposed commoners of Qi and Han, as well as the lands of the three lakes Baiyun, Jingyang, and Guangping.

sentences.zh: 憲宗悉予之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong granted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong granted all of it.

sentences.zh: 復請業南旺湖，以漕渠故不許。

translations.literal: He again requested to exploit Nanwang Lake; because of the Grand Canal this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He again requested to exploit Nanwang Lake, but because of the Grand Canal this was refused.

sentences.zh: 又請漢庶人舊牧馬地，知府趙璜言地歸民間，供稅賦已久，不宜奪。

translations.literal: He again requested the former horse pasture of the deposed Han commoner; Prefect Zhao Huang said the land had long reverted to the populace and supplied tax and corvée; it should not be seized.
translations.idiomatic: He again requested the former horse pasture of the deposed Han commoner. Prefect Zhao Huang said the land had long reverted to the populace and supplied taxes and corvée, and should not be seized.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this advice.

sentences.zh: 正德初，詔王府莊田畝徵銀三分，歲為常。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde an edict fixed at three fen of silver per mu the levy on princely estate fields, to be collected annually as a permanent rule.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengde an edict fixed the levy on princely estate fields at three fen of silver per mu, to be collected annually as a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 見潾奏：「初年，兗州莊田歲畝二十升，獨清河一縣，成化中用少卿宋旻議，歲畝五升。

translations.literal: Jian Lin memorialized: "In earlier years the De princedom's fields in Yanzhou yielded twenty sheng per mu annually; for Qinghe County alone, during Chenghua Vice Minister Song Min's proposal was adopted, making it five sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Lin memorialized, "In earlier years the De princedom's fields in Yanzhou yielded twenty sheng per mu annually. For Qinghe County alone, during Chenghua Vice Minister Song Min's proposal was adopted, reducing it to five sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 若如新詔，臣將無以自給。」
