translations.literal: If the new edict is applied, your subject will have no means to support himself."
translations.idiomatic: If the new edict is applied, your subject will have no means to support himself."

sentences.zh: 戶部執山東水旱相仍，百姓雕敝，宜如詔。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue insisted that in Shandong floods and droughts had followed one upon another and the people were destitute; the edict should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue insisted that in Shandong floods and droughts had followed one upon another and the people were destitute, and that the edict should be followed.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「王何患貧！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Why should the prince worry about poverty!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Why should the prince worry about poverty!

sentences.zh: 其勿許。」

translations.literal: Do not grant this."
translations.idiomatic: Do not grant this."

sentences.zh: 十二年薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 12.

sentences.zh: 子懿王祐榕嗣。

translations.literal: His son Prince Yi You Rong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Yi You Rong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，戶部議核王府所請山場湖陂，斷自宣德以後者皆還官。

translations.literal: During Jiajing the Ministry of Revenue deliberated on auditing the hills, ponds, and marshes requested by princely houses, holding that all granted from Xuande onward should revert to the state.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiajing the Ministry of Revenue deliberated on auditing the hills, ponds, and marshes requested by princely houses, holding that all granted from Xuande onward should revert to the state.

sentences.zh: 詔允行。

translations.literal: An edict approved its implementation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved its implementation.

sentences.zh: 於是山東巡撫都御史邵錫奏德府莊田俱在革中，與祐榕相訐奏，錫持之益急。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shandong Grand Coordinator Shao Xi reported that all the De princedom's estate fields were among those slated for abolition; he and You Rong exchanged accusatory memorials, and Xi pressed the matter all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Shandong Grand Coordinator Shao Xi reported that all the De princedom's estate fields were among those slated for abolition. He and You Rong exchanged accusatory memorials, and Xi pressed the matter all the harder.

sentences.zh: 儀衛司軍額千七百人，逃絕者以余丁補。

translations.literal: The ceremonial guard office had an authorized complement of 1,700 soldiers; deserters were to be replaced with surplus households.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial guard office had an authorized complement of 1,700 soldiers; deserters were to be replaced with surplus households.

sentences.zh: 錫謂非制，檄濟南知府楊撫籍諸補充者勿與餉。

translations.literal: Xi held this was not according to regulation and sent a dispatch to Jinan Prefect Yang Fu ordering that those registered as replacements receive no rations.
translations.idiomatic: Xi held this was not according to regulation and sent a dispatch to Jinan Prefect Yang Fu ordering that those registered as replacements receive no rations.

sentences.zh: 軍校大嘩，毀府門。

translations.literal: The military officers and guards raised a great outcry and destroyed the princely gate.
translations.idiomatic: The military officers and guards raised a great outcry and destroyed the princely gate.

sentences.zh: 詔逮問長史楊穀、楊孟法，戍儀衛副薛寧及軍校陶榮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the arrest and interrogation of chief administrators Yang Gu and Yang Mengfa, banishment of ceremonial guard deputy Xue Ning and military officer Tao Rong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the arrest and interrogation of chief administrators Yang Gu and Yang Mengfa, and the banishment of ceremonial guard deputy Xue Ning and military officer Tao Rong.

sentences.zh: 諭王守侯度，毋徇群小滋多事。

translations.literal: The prince was admonished to maintain restraint and not indulge petty men to stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was admonished to maintain restraint and not indulge petty men to stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 議者謂錫故激致其罪，不盡祐榕過雲。

translations.literal: Commentators held that Xi had deliberately provoked their crimes and did not wholly reflect You Rong's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that Xi had deliberately provoked their crimes and did not wholly reflect You Rong's faults.

sentences.zh: 此十一年八月事。

translations.literal: This was a matter of the eighth month of the eleventh year.
translations.idiomatic: This was a matter of the eighth month of the eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 至十八年，涇、徽二王復請得所革莊田，祐榕援以為請。

translations.literal: By the eighteenth year the Princes of Jing and Hui again requested restoration of their abolished estate fields; You Rong cited this precedent in his own petition.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighteenth year the Princes of Jing and Hui again requested restoration of their abolished estate fields, and You Rong cited this precedent in his own petition.

sentences.zh: 詔仍與三湖地，使自徵其課。

translations.literal: An edict restored the three lakes lands, allowing him to collect the dues himself.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored the three lakes lands, allowing him to collect the dues himself.

sentences.zh: 其年薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died.

sentences.zh: 孫恭王載墱嗣，萬歷二年薨。

translations.literal: His grandson Prince Gong Zai Peng succeeded; he died in the second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Prince Gong Zai Peng succeeded and died in Wanli 2.

sentences.zh: 子定王翊館嗣，十六年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Ding Yi Guan succeeded; he died in the sixteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Ding Yi Guan succeeded and died in year 16.

sentences.zh: 子常潔嗣，崇禎五年薨。

translations.literal: His son Chang Jie succeeded; he died in the fifth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang Jie succeeded and died in Chongzhen 5.

sentences.zh: 世子由樞嗣，十二年正月，大清兵克濟南，見執。

translations.literal: The heir You Shu succeeded; in the first month of the twelfth year Qing troops captured Jinan and he was taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: The heir You Shu succeeded. In the first month of year 12 Qing troops captured Jinan and he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 見湜，英宗第三子。

translations.literal: Jian Shi was the third son of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Shi was Emperor Yingzong's third son.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 復辟後，不復追贈。

translations.literal: After the restoration, he was not posthumously ennobled again.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingzong's restoration to the throne, no further posthumous honors were conferred on him.

sentences.zh: 許悼王見淳，英宗第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Dao of Xu, Jian Chun, was the fourth son of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dao of Xu, Jian Chun, was Emperor Yingzong's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in Jingtai 3.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the third year of Jingtai.

sentences.zh: 明年薨。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 禮臣請用親王禮葬。

translations.literal: The ritual officials asked to bury him with the rites of a full prince.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of rites requested a funeral according to the full rites for an imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 帝以王幼，殺其制。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the prince was young, reduced the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering how young the prince had been, scaled back the prescribed rites.

sentences.zh: 秀懷王見澍，英宗第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Xiu, Jian Shu, was the fifth son of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Xiu, Jian Shu, was Emperor Yingzong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 生於南宮，天順元年封。

translations.literal: Born in the Southern Palace, he was enfeoffed in Tianshun 1.
translations.idiomatic: Born in the Southern Palace, he was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 成化六年就藩汝寧。

translations.literal: In Chenghua 6 he went to his fief at Runing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chenghua he took up his fief at Runing.

sentences.zh: 長史劉誠獻《千秋日鑒錄》，見澍朝夕誦之。

translations.literal: Chief steward Liu Cheng presented the 《Records for Days of a Thousand Autumns》; Jian Shu recited it morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Chief steward Liu Cheng presented the 《Records for Days of a Thousand Autumns》, which Jian Shu recited every morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 就藩時，慮途中擾民，令並日行。

translations.literal: When he went to his fief, fearing that the journey would disturb the people, he ordered that the whole route be traveled in one day.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed for his fief, fearing that the procession would burden the people along the way, he ordered that the entire journey be completed in a single day.

sentences.zh: 王居隘，左右請遷文廟廣之。

translations.literal: The prince's residence was cramped; those around him asked to move the Confucian temple and expand it.
translations.idiomatic: His residence was cramped, and his attendants proposed relocating the Confucian temple to enlarge it.

sentences.zh: 見澍不聽，曰：「居近學宮，時時聞糸玄頌聲，顧不美乎！」

translations.literal: Jian Shu would not listen and said: "Living near the academy, one constantly hears the sounds of strings and recitation -- is that not fine!"
translations.idiomatic: Jian Shu refused and said, "Living beside the academy, I can always hear the sounds of strings and recitation from the students -- is that not a delight!"

sentences.zh: 論《書》至《西伯戡黎》，長史誠主吳氏說，曰：「戡黎者，武王也。」

translations.literal: When they discussed the 《Book of Documents》 down to the 《King Wu's Campaign against Li》, Chief Steward Cheng upheld the Wu school and said: "The one who campaigned against Li was King Wu."
translations.idiomatic: When their discussion of the 《Book of Documents》 reached the chapter 《King Wu's Campaign against Li》, Chief Steward Liu Cheng took the Wu-school view and said: "The conqueror of Li was King Wu."

sentences.zh: 右長史趙銳主孔氏說，曰：「實文王事。」

translations.literal: The right chief steward Zhao Rui upheld the Kong school and said: "It was in fact King Wen's affair."
translations.idiomatic: Right chief steward Zhao Rui held to the Kong-school view and said, "It was in fact an act of King Wen."

sentences.zh: 爭之失色。

translations.literal: They argued until their faces changed color.
translations.idiomatic: They argued until both men flushed with anger.

sentences.zh: 見澍曰：「經義未有定論，不嫌往復。

translations.literal: Jian Shu said: "The meaning of the classics has no settled conclusion; there is no harm in going back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Shu said, "The classics admit no final verdict on this point; there is no shame in debating back and forth.

sentences.zh: 今若此，非先皇帝簡二先生意也。」

translations.literal: If it is like this now, it is not what the late emperor intended in selecting the two masters."
translations.idiomatic: To quarrel like this now is not what the late emperor intended when he chose you two as teachers."

sentences.zh: 成化八年薨。

translations.literal: He died in Chenghua 8.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 無子，封除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son, and the princely line was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 崇簡王見澤，英宗第六子。

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Chong, Jian Ze, was the sixth son of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Chong, Jian Ze, was Emperor Yingzong's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 生於南宮，天順元年封。

translations.literal: Born in the Southern Palace, he was enfeoffed in Tianshun 1.
translations.idiomatic: Born in the Southern Palace, he was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 成化十年就藩汝寧，故秀邸也。

translations.literal: In Chenghua 10 he went to his fief at Runing, the former residence of Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Chenghua he took up his fief at Runing, which had been the seat of the Prince of Xiu.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年七月，皇太后春秋高，思一見王，帝特敕召之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Hongzhi 8, the empress dowager was advanced in years and wished to see the prince once; the emperor specially ordered him summoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Hongzhi, the empress dowager, now elderly, longed to see the prince once more, and the emperor issued a special summons.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書倪嶽言：「數年來三王之國，道路供億，民力殫竭。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Ni Yue said: "In recent years the establishment of three princes in their fiefs has exhausted the people with supplies along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Ni Yue argued, "In recent years the departures of three princes for their fiefs have drained the people dry with provisioning along every road.

sentences.zh: 今召王復來，往返勞費，兼水溢旱蝗，舟車所經，恐有他虞。

translations.literal: Now to summon the prince to come again, the toil and expense of the round trip, together with floods, drought, and locusts -- wherever boats and carts pass, I fear there may be other troubles.
translations.idiomatic: To summon the prince back now would impose the cost and hardship of another round trip, and with floods, drought, and locusts abroad, every route by land and water may bring unforeseen dangers.

sentences.zh: 親王入朝，雖有故事，自宣德來，已鮮舉行。

translations.literal: An imperial prince coming to court, though there is precedent, has rarely been done since Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: Although princes have occasionally attended court in the past, such visits have been rare since the Xuande reign.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，襄王奉詔來朝，雖篤敦敘之恩，實塞疑讒之隙，非故事也。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored, the Prince of Xiang came to court by imperial command; though it deepened bonds of kinship, it in fact closed gaps of suspicion and slander -- it was not precedent."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, the Prince of Xiang came to court by edict; though that visit strengthened fraternal ties, it was really meant to close off suspicion and slander, not to set a precedent."

sentences.zh: 大學士徐溥亦以為言。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xu Pu also spoke to the same effect.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xu Pu made the same argument.

sentences.zh: 帝重違太后意，不允。

translations.literal: The emperor, loath to go against the empress dowager's wish, did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to override the empress dowager's wishes, the emperor would not consent.

sentences.zh: 既而言官交章及之，乃已。

translations.literal: Afterward censorial officials submitted memorial after memorial on the matter, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon censorial officials submitted a stream of memorials on the subject, and the summons was canceled.

sentences.zh: 十八年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the eighteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 子靖王祐樒嗣，正德六年薨。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Jing, You Si, succeeded; he died in Zhengde 6.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Jing, You Si, succeeded him and died in the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 子恭王厚耀嗣。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Gong, Hou Yao, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Gong, Hou Yao, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 三王並有賢名，而靖王尤孝友。

translations.literal: All three princes had reputations for worth, and Prince Jing was especially filial and fraternal.
translations.idiomatic: All three princes enjoyed reputations for virtue, and Prince Jing was especially noted for filial piety and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十六年，厚耀薨。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 16, Hou Yao died.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yao died in the sixteenth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 子莊王載境嗣，三十六年薨。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Zhuang, Zai Jing, succeeded; he died in the thirty-sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Zhuang, Zai Jing, succeeded him and died in the thirty-sixth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 子端王翊𨰜嗣，萬歷三十八年薨。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Duan, Yi Yue, succeeded; he died in Wanli 38.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Duan, Yi Yue, succeeded him and died in the thirty-eighth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 孫由樻嗣。

translations.literal: His grandson You Ku succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson You Ku succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年閏十一月，李自成陷汝寧，執由樻去，偽封襄陽伯，令諭降州縣之未下者。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month of Chongzhen 15, Li Zicheng took Runing, seized You Ku, falsely enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xiangyang, and ordered him to persuade the prefectures and counties not yet fallen to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month of the fifteenth year of Chongzhen, Li Zicheng captured Runing, took You Ku prisoner, gave him the bogus title Marquis of Xiangyang, and ordered him to urge the remaining prefectures and counties to submit.

sentences.zh: 由樻不從，殺之於泌陽城。

translations.literal: You Ku would not obey and was killed in Biyang city.
translations.idiomatic: You Ku refused, and Li Zicheng had him executed in Biyang.

sentences.zh: 弟河陽王由材、世子慈煇等皆遇害。

translations.literal: His younger brother, the Prince of Heyang, You Cai, the heir Cihui, and others all met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, Prince of Heyang You Cai, the heir Cihui, and others were all killed as well.

sentences.zh: 吉簡王見浚，英宗第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Ji, Jian Jun, was the seventh son of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Ji, Jian Jun, was Emperor Yingzong's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 生於南宮。

translations.literal: He was born in the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the Southern Palace.

sentences.zh: 天順元年封，時甫二歲。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in Tianshun 1, when he was only two years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianshun, when he was only two.

sentences.zh: 成化十三年就藩長沙，刻《先聖圖》及《尚書》於嶽麓書院，以授學者。

translations.literal: In Chenghua 13 he went to his fief at Changsha, carved the 《Illustrations of the Ancient Sage》 and the 《Book of Documents》 at Yuelu Academy, and used them to instruct scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Chenghua he took up his fief at Changsha, had the 《Illustrations of the Ancient Sage》 and the 《Book of Documents》 carved at Yuelu Academy, and used them to teach students.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年薨。

translations.literal: He died in Jiajing 6.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 孫定王厚冒嗣。

translations.literal: His grandson, Prince Ding, Houyang Mao, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson, Prince Ding, Houyang Mao, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 請湘潭商稅益邸租，不許。

translations.literal: He asked that Xiangtan commercial taxes supplement the princely rent; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to have Xiangtan's commercial taxes added to his princely income, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 十八年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the eighteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 子端王載均由光化王嗣，四十年薨。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Duan, Zai Jun, succeeded from the Prince of Guanghua; he died in the fortieth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Duan, Zai Jun, succeeded from the line of the Prince of Guanghua and died in the fortieth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 子莊王翊鎮嗣，隆慶四年薨。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Zhuang, Yi Zhen, succeeded; he died in Longqing 4.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Zhuang, Yi Zhen, succeeded him and died in the fourth year of Longqing.

sentences.zh: 無子，庶兄宣王翊鑾由龍陽王嗣，萬歷四十六年薨。

translations.literal: Having no son, his elder half-brother, Prince Xuan, Yi Luan, succeeded from the Prince of Longyang; he died in Wanli 46.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son, so his elder half-brother, Prince Xuan, Yi Luan, succeeded from the line of the Prince of Longyang and died in the forty-sixth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 孫由棟嗣，崇禎九年薨。

translations.literal: His grandson You Dong succeeded; he died in Chongzhen 9.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson You Dong succeeded him and died in the ninth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 子慈煃嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cihui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cihui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，張獻忠入湖南，同惠王走衡州，隨入粵。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Zhang Xianzhong entered Hunan; together with the Prince of Hui he fled to Hengzhou and then entered Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Zhang Xianzhong invaded Hunan; Cihui fled with the Prince of Hui to Hengzhou and then on into Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 國亡後，死於緬甸。

translations.literal: After the dynasty fell, he died in Burma.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynasty collapsed, he died in Burma.

sentences.zh: 忻穆王見治，英宗第八子。

translations.literal: Prince Mu of Xin, Jian Zhi, was the eighth son of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mu of Xin, Jian Zhi, was Emperor Yingzong's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 成化二年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in Chenghua 2.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the second year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 未就藩，八年薨。

translations.literal: Before going to his fief, he died in the eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his fief, he died in the eighth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 無後。

translations.literal: He had no descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heirs.

sentences.zh: 徽莊王見沛，英宗第九子。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang of Hui, Jian Pei, was the ninth son of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuang of Hui, Jian Pei, was Emperor Yingzong's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 成化二年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in Chenghua 2.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the second year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 十七年就藩鈞州。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he went to his fief at Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the reign he took up his fief at Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 承奉司自置吏，左布政使徐恪革之，見沛以聞。

translations.literal: The service bureau appointed its own officials on its own authority; Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Xu Ke abolished this, and Jian Pei reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The princely service bureau had been appointing its own officials; Left provincial administration commissioner Xu Ke abolished the practice, and Jian Pei reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 憲宗書諭王：「置吏，非制也，恪無罪。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong wrote to instruct the prince: "Appointing officials is not according to regulation; Ke is not guilty."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong wrote to the prince, "Appointing officials on your own authority is not permitted by statute; Xu Ke is not at fault."

sentences.zh: 正德元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in Zhengde 1.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 子簡王祐枱嗣，嘉靖四年薨。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Jian, You Tai, succeeded; he died in Jiajing 4.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Jian, You Tai, succeeded him and died in the fourth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 子恭王厚爵嗣，二十九年薨。

translations.literal: His son, Prince Gong, Houyang Jue, succeeded; he died in the twenty-ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Gong, Houyang Jue, succeeded him and died in the twenty-ninth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 子浦城王載埨嗣。

translations.literal: His son, the Prince of Pucheng, Zai Kun, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince of Pucheng Zai Kun, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 初，厚爵好琴，斫琴者與知州陳吉交惡，厚爵庇之，劾吉，逮詔獄。

translations.literal: At first Houyang Jue loved the zither; a zither maker had a bitter quarrel with prefect Chen Ji, and Houyang Jue sheltered him, impeached Ji, and had him seized and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Houyang Jue was devoted to the zither; when a lute maker fell out with Prefect Chen Ji, Houyang Jue shielded the craftsman, impeached Chen Ji, and had him thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 都御史駱昂、御史王三聘白吉冤。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Luo Ang and censor Wang Sanpin declared Ji's innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Luo Ang and investigating censor Wang Sanpin declared that Chen Ji had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，並逮之，昂杖死，三聘、吉俱戍邊。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, seized them all together; Ang was beaten to death, and Sanpin and Ji were both sent to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had them all arrested; Luo Ang was beaten to death, while Wang Sanpin and Chen Ji were both banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 議者不直厚爵。

translations.literal: Those who discussed the matter did not side with Houyang Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion did not side with Houyang Jue.

sentences.zh: 時方士陶仲文有寵於世宗，厚爵厚結之。

translations.literal: At the time the Daoist adept Tao Zhongwen had favor with Emperor Shizong; Houyang Jue cultivated close ties with him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Daoist adept Tao Zhongwen enjoyed Emperor Shizong's favor, and Houyang Jue cultivated a close alliance with him.

sentences.zh: 仲文具言王忠敬奉道。

translations.literal: Zhongwen fully stated that the prince was loyal, reverent, and devoted to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Zhongwen repeatedly praised the prince's loyal and devout service to the Way.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，封厚爵太清輔元宣化真人，予金印。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and enfeoffed Houyang Jue as the Perfected Man Who Assists the Origin and Spreads Transformation in the Great Clarity, granting a gold seal.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor ennobled Houyang Jue as Perfected Man of Great Clarity, Assistant to the Origin and Spreader of Transformation, and granted him a gold seal.

sentences.zh: 及載埨嗣王，益以奉道自媚於帝，命綰其父真人印。

translations.literal: When Zai Kun succeeded as prince, he all the more used devotion to the Way to ingratiate himself with the emperor and was ordered to keep his father's seal as a perfected man.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai Kun succeeded to the princely title, he curried favor with the emperor all the more through religious devotion and was ordered to keep his father's seal as a perfected man.

sentences.zh: 南陽人梁高輔自言能導引服食，載埨用其術和藥，命高輔因仲文以進帝。

translations.literal: Liang Gaofu of Nanyang claimed he could guide breath and ingest elixirs; Zai Kun used his techniques to compound drugs and ordered Gaofu to present them to the emperor through Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Gaofu of Nanyang claimed to know techniques of breath cultivation and elixir consumption; Zai Kun used his methods to compound drugs and had Gaofu present them to the emperor through Tao Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 封高輔通妙散人，載埨清微翊教輔化忠孝真人。

translations.literal: Gaofu was enfeoffed as the Recluse of Penetrating Wonder; Zai Kun was made the Perfected Man of Pure Subtlety Who Assists in Teaching, Supports Transformation, and Embodies Loyalty and Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Gaofu was ennobled Recluse of Penetrating Wonder, and Zai Kun was made Perfected Man of Pure Subtlety, Assistant in Teaching, Supporter of Transformation, and Embodiment of Loyalty and Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 載埨遂益恣，壞民屋，作臺榭苑囿。

translations.literal: Zai Kun then became all the more unrestrained, destroying people's houses and building terraces, pavilions, gardens, and parks.
translations.idiomatic: Zai Kun then grew ever more reckless, tearing down commoners' homes to build terraces, pavilions, gardens, and pleasure grounds.

sentences.zh: 庫官王章諫，杖殺之。

translations.literal: The treasury officer Wang Zhang remonstrated and was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury officer Wang Zhang tried to dissuade him and was flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 嘗微服之揚州、鳳陽，為邏者所獲，羈留三月，走歸。

translations.literal: He once went in plain dress to Yangzhou and Fengyang, was seized by patrol guards, detained for three months, and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: He once traveled incognito to Yangzhou and Fengyang, was caught by patrol guards, held for three months, and then escaped home.

sentences.zh: 時高輔被上寵，不復親載埨，載埨銜之。

translations.literal: At the time Gaofu enjoyed the emperor's favor and no longer kept company with Zai Kun; Zai Kun bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Liang Gaofu had the emperor's favor and no longer kept close ties with Zai Kun, who resented him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 已而為帝取藥不得，求載埨舊所蓄者，載埨不與，而與仲文。

translations.literal: Later, when drugs could not be obtained for the emperor, the emperor sought those Zai Kun had formerly stored; Zai Kun would not give them but gave them to Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor later needed elixirs and could not obtain them, he asked for Zai Kun's old stock; Zai Kun refused him but gave the drugs to Tao Zhongwen instead.

sentences.zh: 高輔大恨，乘間言載埨私往南中，與他過失。

translations.literal: Gaofu hated this deeply and seized an opportunity to say that Zai Kun had secretly gone south and report his other faults.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Gaofu hated this and seized his chance to accuse Zai Kun of secretly traveling south and of other misconduct.

sentences.zh: 帝疑之，奪真人印。

translations.literal: The emperor grew suspicious and stripped away the seal of the perfected man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew suspicious and revoked his seal as a perfected man.

sentences.zh: 仲文知釁已成，不復敢言。

translations.literal: Zhongwen knew the breach had already formed and no longer dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Zhongwen saw that the breach was beyond repair and dared not intervene.

sentences.zh: 三十五年有民耿安者，奏載埨奪其女，下按治。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year a commoner named Geng An memorialized that Zai Kun had seized his daughter, and the case was sent down for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year a commoner named Geng An petitioned that Zai Kun had abducted his daughter, and the case was referred for investigation.

sentences.zh: 有司因發其諸不法事。

translations.literal: The officials thereupon uncovered his various unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: The investigating officials then uncovered a string of his illegal acts.

sentences.zh: 獄成，降為庶人，錮高墻。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, he was reduced to commoner status and imprisoned within high walls.
translations.idiomatic: Once the case was complete, he was stripped of rank, reduced to commoner status, and imprisoned within high walls.

sentences.zh: 時載埨居宮中，所司防守嚴，獄詞不得聞。

translations.literal: At the time Zai Kun dwelt within the palace; the offices guarding him were strict, and he could not hear the words of the case.
translations.idiomatic: Zai Kun remained inside the palace under tight guard and never learned what the investigation had found.

sentences.zh: 及帝遣內臣同撫按至，始大懼。

translations.literal: When the emperor dispatched inner eunuchs together with the provincial governor and censor, he at last grew greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the emperor sent palace eunuchs along with provincial investigators did he finally panic.

sentences.zh: 登樓，望龍亭後有紅板輿，嘆曰：「吾不能自明，徒生奚為！」

translations.literal: He ascended a tower, saw behind the Dragon Pavilion a red-planked palanquin, and sighed: "I cannot clear myself; what is the use of clinging to life!"
translations.idiomatic: He climbed a tower, saw a red palanquin waiting behind the Dragon Pavilion, and sighed: "If I cannot clear my name, what point is there in living on?"

sentences.zh: 遂自縊死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 妃沈氏、次妃林氏爭取帛自縊。

translations.literal: Consort Shen and secondary consort Lin struggled to seize silk and hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Shen and secondary consort Lin fought over the silk cord and hanged themselves as well.

sentences.zh: 子安陽王翊锜、萬善王翊鈁並革爵，及未封子女，皆遷開封，聽周王約束，國除。

translations.literal: His sons Prince of Anyang Yi Qi and Prince of Wanshan Yi Fang were both stripped of rank; together with unenfeoffed sons and daughters, all were moved to Kaifeng to be kept under the Prince of Zhou's control, and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Prince of Anyang Yi Qi and Prince of Wanshan Yi Fang were both stripped of rank; his unenfeoffed children were relocated to Kaifeng under the Prince of Zhou's supervision, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝一子，懷獻太子見濟。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing had one son, the Crown Prince Huai Xian Jian Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing had one son: Crown Prince Huai Xian, Jian Ji.

sentences.zh: 母杭妃。

translations.literal: His mother was Consort Hang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Consort Hang.

sentences.zh: 始為郕王世子。

translations.literal: At first he was heir to the Prince of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally been heir to the Prince of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，皇太后命立憲宗為皇太子，而以郕王監國。

translations.literal: When the Ying Emperor was taken north, the empress dowager ordered that Xianzong be established as crown prince while the Prince of Cheng supervised the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ying Emperor was captured on the northern campaign, the empress dowager named Xianzong crown prince and had the Prince of Cheng supervise the realm.

sentences.zh: 及郕王即位，心欲以見濟代太子，而難於發，皇后汪氏又力以為不可，遲回久之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Cheng ascended the throne, in his heart he wished to replace the crown prince with Jian Ji but found it hard to bring up; Empress Wang also strongly held that it could not be done, and he hesitated for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Cheng took the throne, he wanted to replace the crown prince with Jian Ji but could not bring himself to act; Empress Wang also strongly opposed the move, and he wavered for a long time.

sentences.zh: 太監王誠、舒良為帝謀，先賜大學士陳循、高穀百金，侍郎江淵、王一寧、蕭鎡，學士商輅半之，用以緘其口，然猶未發也。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Wang Cheng and Shu Liang plotted for the emperor; first they bestowed one hundred taels of gold on grand secretaries Chen Xun and Gao Gu, and half that on vice ministers Jiang Yuan, Wang Yining, and Xiao Zan and academician Shang Lu, to seal their mouths, yet still he had not acted.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs Wang Cheng and Shu Liang plotted on the emperor's behalf, bribing Grand Secretaries Chen Xun and Gao Gu with a hundred taels of gold each and half that to Vice Ministers Jiang Yuan, Wang Yining, and Xiao Zan and Academician Shang Lu to buy their silence, yet the emperor still held back.

sentences.zh: 會廣西土官都指揮使黃矰以私怨戕其弟思明知府岡，滅其家，所司聞於朝。

translations.literal: It happened that the native official commander Huang Zeng of Guangxi, out of private resentment, killed his younger brother Siming prefect Gang and exterminated his household; the offices reported it to court.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Huang Zeng, a native-official commander in Guangxi, killed his younger brother Siming Prefect Gang in a private vendetta and wiped out his household; the case was reported to court.

sentences.zh: 矰懼罪，急遣千戶袁洪走京師，上疏勸帝早與親信大臣密定大計，易建東宮，以一中外之心，絕覬覦之望。

translations.literal: Zeng feared punishment and urgently sent the chiliarch Yuan Hong to rush to the capital and submit a memorial urging the emperor early to settle the great plan secretly with trusted grand ministers, quickly to change the Eastern Palace, unify the hearts of court and realm, and cut off hopes of usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, Huang Zeng urgently sent chiliarch Yuan Hong to the capital with a memorial urging the emperor to settle the succession in secret with trusted ministers, install a new heir apparent, unify court and country, and forestall any bid for the throne.

sentences.zh: 疏入，景帝大喜，亟下廷臣會議，且令釋矰罪，進階都督。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Jing Emperor was greatly pleased, immediately ordered the court ministers to confer, and also ordered Zeng's crime released and his rank advanced to commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor was delighted, immediately ordered a court conference, pardoned Huang Zeng, and promoted him to commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時景泰三年四月也。

translations.literal: It was the fourth month of the third year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fourth month of Jingtai 3.

sentences.zh: 疏下之明日，禮部尚書胡濙，侍郎薩琦、鄒幹集文武群臣廷議。

translations.literal: The day after the memorial was issued, Minister of Rites Hu Ying and vice ministers Sa Qi and Zou Gan assembled civil and military ministers at court for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The day after the memorial was circulated, Minister of Rites Hu Ying and Vice Ministers Sa Qi and Zou Gan convened the full civil and military court for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 眾相顧，莫敢發言。

translations.literal: The multitude looked at one another; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled officials looked at one another in silence; no one dared speak first.

sentences.zh: 惟都給事中李侃、林聰，御史朱英以為不可。

translations.literal: Only supervising secretaries Li Kan and Lin Cong and censor Zhu Ying held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Only supervising secretaries Li Kan and Lin Cong and censor Zhu Ying declared the move unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王直亦有難色。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi also showed difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi also looked deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 司禮太監興安歷聲曰：「此事不可已，即以為不可者，勿署名，無持兩端。」

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonies eunuch Xing An said in a stern voice: "This matter cannot be left undone; those who hold it cannot be done need not sign; do not hold two positions."
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonies eunuch Xing An said sharply: "This must be done. Whoever objects need not sign; there will be no fence-sitting."

sentences.zh: 群臣皆唯唯署議。

translations.literal: The ministers all murmured assent and signed the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all murmured agreement and signed the proposal.

sentences.zh: 於是濙苳等暨魏國公徐承宗，寧陽侯陳懋，安遠侯柳溥，武清侯石亨，成安侯郭晟，定西侯蔣琬，駙馬都尉薛桓，襄城伯李瑾，武進伯朱瑛，平鄉伯陳輔，安鄉伯張寧，都督孫鏜、張軏、楊俊，都督同知田禮、範廣、過興、衛穎，都督僉事張兒、劉深、張通、郭瑛、劉鑒、張義，錦衣衛指揮同知畢旺、曹敬，指揮僉事林福，吏部尚書王直，戶部尚書文淵閣大學士陳循，工部尚書東閣大學士高穀，吏部尚書何文淵，戶部尚書金濂，兵部尚書于謙，刑部尚書俞士悅，左都御史王文、王翺、楊善，吏部侍郎江淵、俞山、項文耀，戶部侍郎劉中敷、沈翼、蕭鎡，禮部侍郎王一寧，兵部侍郎李賢，刑部侍郎周瑄，工部侍郎趙榮、張敏，通政使李錫，通政欒惲、王復，參議馮貫，諸寺卿蕭維禎、許彬、蔣守約、齊整、李賓，少卿張固、習嘉言、李宗周、蔚能、陳誠、黃士俊、張翔、齊政，寺丞李茂、李希安、柴望、酈鏞、楊詢、王溢，翰林學士商輅，六科都給事中李讚、李侃、李春、蘇霖、林聰、張文質，十三道御史王震、朱英、塗謙、丁泰亨、強弘、劉琚、陸厚、原傑、嚴樞、沈義、楊宜、王驥、左鼎上言：「陛下膺天明命，中興邦家，統緒之傳宜歸聖子，黃矰奏是。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Hu Ying and the others, together with Duke of Wei Xu Chengzong, Marquis of Ningyang Chen Mao, Marquis of Anyuan Liu Pu, Marquis of Wuqing Shi Heng, Marquis of Cheng'an Guo Sheng, Marquis of Dingxi Jiang Wan, Commandant of Horse Xue Huan, Count of Xiangcheng Li Jin, Count of Wujin Zhu Ying, Count of Pingxiang Chen Fu, and Count of Anxiang Zhang Ning; commanders Sun Tang, Zhang Yu, and Yang Jun; vice commanders Tian Li, Fan Guang, Guo Xing, and Wei Ying; assistant commanders Zhang Er, Liu Shen, Zhang Tong, Guo Ying, Liu Jian, and Zhang Yi; assistant commanders of the Embroidered Uniform Guard Bi Wang and Cao Jing; guard assistant commander Lin Fu; Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi, Minister of Revenue and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth Chen Xun, Minister of Works and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion Gao Gu, Minister of Personnel He Wenyuan, Minister of Revenue Jin Lian, Minister of War Yu Qian, and Minister of Justice Yu Shiyue; censors-in-chief Wang Wen, Wang Ao, and Yang Shan; vice ministers Jiang Yuan, Yu Shan, and Xiang Wenyao; vice ministers Liu Zhongfu, Shen Yi, and Xiao Zan; Vice Minister of Rites Wang Yining, Vice Minister of War Li Xian, Vice Minister of Justice Zhou Xuan, and vice ministers Zhao Rong and Zhang Min; transmission commissioner Li Xi, transmission officials Luan Yun and Wang Fu, and adviser Feng Guan; ministers of the various courts Xiao Weizhen, Xu Bin, Jiang Shouyue, Qi Zheng, and Li Bin; vice ministers Zhang Gu, Xi Jiayan, Li Zongzhou, Wei Neng, Chen Cheng, Huang Shijun, Zhang Xiang, and Qi Zheng; court directors Li Mao, Li Xi'an, Chai Wang, Li Yong, Yang Xun, and Wang Yi; Hanlin academician Shang Lu; supervising secretaries of the six offices Li Zan, Li Kan, Li Chun, Su Lin, Lin Cong, and Zhang Wenzhi; and censors of the thirteen circuits Wang Zhen, Zhu Ying, Tu Qian, Ding Taiheng, Qiang Hong, Liu Ju, Lu Hou, Yuan Jie, Yan Shu, Shen Yi, Yang Yi, Wang Ji, and Zuo Ding submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has received Heaven's clear mandate and revived the state and house; the transmission of the imperial line ought to return to a holy son; Huang Zeng's memorial is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Hu Ying and the others, together with Duke of Wei Xu Chengzong, Marquis of Ningyang Chen Mao, Marquis of Anyuan Liu Pu, Marquis of Wuqing Shi Heng, Marquis of Cheng'an Guo Sheng, Marquis of Dingxi Jiang Wan, Commandant of Horse Xue Huan, Count of Xiangcheng Li Jin, Count of Wujin Zhu Ying, Count of Pingxiang Chen Fu, and Count of Anxiang Zhang Ning; the transmission of the imperial line ought to return to the sacred son. Huang Zeng's memorial is correct."

sentences.zh: 制曰：「可。

translations.literal: The rescript said: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read: "Approved.

sentences.zh: 禮部具儀，擇日以聞。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites shall prepare the rites and choose a day to report."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites was ordered to prepare the rites and report the chosen date."

sentences.zh: 即日，簡置東宮官，公孤詹事僚屬悉備。

translations.literal: That same day, Eastern Palace offices were selected and appointed; the three dukes, tutors, and attendants were all complete.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Eastern Palace staff was appointed, with tutors and attendants fully in place.

sentences.zh: 五月，廢汪後，立杭妃為皇后，更封太子為沂王，立見濟為太子。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Empress Wang was deposed; Consort Hang was established as empress; the crown prince was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Yi; and Jian Ji was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Empress Wang was deposed, Consort Hang was made empress, the former crown prince was demoted to Prince of Yi, and Jian Ji was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「天佑下民作之君，實遺安於四海；

translations.literal: The edict said: "Heaven blesses the people and makes for them a ruler, truly leaving peace to the four seas;
translations.idiomatic: The edict proclaimed: "Heaven blesses the people and sets over them a ruler, that peace may reach the four seas;

sentences.zh: 父有天下傳之子，斯本固於萬年。」

translations.literal: a father who possesses the realm transmits it to his son; thus the root is firm for ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: a father who holds the realm passes it to his son, so that the foundation may stand for ten thousand years."

sentences.zh: 大赦天下，令百官朔望朝太子，賜諸親王、公主、邊鎮、文武內外群臣，又加賜陳循、高穀、江淵、王一寧、蕭鎡、商輅各黃金五十兩。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm; officials were ordered to attend upon the crown prince at the new and full moon; princes, princesses, frontier garrisons, and civil and military ministers within and without were all granted gifts; Chen Xun, Gao Gu, Jiang Yuan, Wang Yining, Xiao Zan, and Shang Lu were each additionally granted fifty taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed; officials were ordered to attend the crown prince on the first and fifteenth of each month; princes, princesses, frontier garrisons, and the whole civil and military establishment received gifts; and Chen Xun, Gao Gu, Jiang Yuan, Wang Yining, Xiao Zan, and Shang Lu each received an additional fifty taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 四年二月乙未，太子冠。

translations.literal: On the yimwei day of the second month of the fourth year, the crown prince received the capping rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimwei day of the second month in the fourth year, the crown prince underwent the capping ceremony.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以御史張鵬言，簡東宮師傅講讀官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on censor Zhang Peng's recommendation, tutors and lecturers of the Eastern Palace were selected.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on censor Zhang Peng's recommendation, tutors and lecturers for the Eastern Palace were appointed.

sentences.zh: 越四日，太子薨，謚曰懷獻，葬西山。

translations.literal: Four days later the crown prince died; his posthumous title was Huai Xian, and he was buried at Western Hills.
translations.idiomatic: Four days later the crown prince died; he was posthumously titled Huai Xian and buried at the Western Hills.

sentences.zh: 天順元年，降稱懷獻世子，諸建議易儲者皆得罪。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun he was reduced in title to Heir Huai Xian, and all who had proposed changing the heir were punished.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 1 he was demoted to heir Huai Xian, and all who had advocated changing the succession were punished.

sentences.zh: 憲宗十四子。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong had fourteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong had fourteen sons.

sentences.zh: 萬貴妃生皇第一子。

translations.literal: Consort Wan bore the emperor's first son.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wan bore the emperor's first son.

sentences.zh: 柏賢妃生悼恭太子祐極。

translations.literal: Consort Bo Xian bore the Crown Prince Daogong You Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Bo Xian bore Crown Prince Daogong You Ji.

sentences.zh: 紀太后生孝宗。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ji bore Emperor Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ji bore Emperor Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 邵太后生興獻帝祐杬、岐王祐棆、雍王祐枟。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Shao bore Emperor Xingxian You Yuan, Prince Qi You Lin, and Prince Yong You Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Shao bore Emperor Xingxian You Yuan, Prince Qi You Lin, and Prince Yong You Cong.

sentences.zh: 張德妃生益王祐檳、衡王祐楎、汝王祐梈。

translations.literal: Consort Zhang De bore Prince Yi You Bin, Prince Heng You Yang, and Prince Ru You Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang De bore Prince Yi You Bin, Prince Heng You Yang, and Prince Ru You Bing.

sentences.zh: 姚安妃生壽王祐楮。

translations.literal: Consort Yao An bore Prince Shou You Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yao An bore Prince Shou You Chu.

sentences.zh: 楊恭妃生涇王祐橓、申王祐楷。

translations.literal: Consort Yang Gong bore Prince Jing You Fen and Prince Shen You Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang Gong bore Prince Jing You Fen and Prince Shen You Kai.

sentences.zh: 潘端妃生榮王祐樞。

translations.literal: Consort Pan Duan bore Prince Rong You Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Pan Duan bore Prince Rong You Shu.

sentences.zh: 王敬妃生皇第十子。

translations.literal: Consort Wang Jing bore the emperor's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang Jing bore the emperor's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 第一子、第十子皆未名殤。

translations.literal: The first son and the tenth son both died unnamed in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: The first son and the tenth son both died in infancy without receiving names.

sentences.zh: 悼恭太子祐極，憲宗次子。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Daogong You Ji was the second son of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Daogong You Ji was Emperor Xianzong's second son.

sentences.zh: 成化七年立為皇太子薨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chenghua he was established as crown prince and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was named crown prince in Chenghua 7 and died in the same year.

sentences.zh: 岐惠王祐棆，憲宗第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Hui of Qi You Lin was the fifth son of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui of Qi You Lin was Emperor Xianzong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年與益、衡、雍三王同日封。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua he was enfeoffed on the same day as the three princes of Yi, Heng, and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 23 he was enfeoffed on the same day as the Princes of Yi, Heng, and Yong.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年之藩德安。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Hongzhi he went to his fief at De'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 8 he took up his fief at De'an.

sentences.zh: 十四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 無子，封除。

translations.literal: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: With no heir, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 益端王祐檳，憲宗第六子。

translations.literal: Prince Duan of Yi You Bin was the sixth son of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duan of Yi You Bin was Emperor Xianzong's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年之藩建昌，故荊邸也。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Hongzhi he went to his fief at Jianchang, the former residence of the Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 8 he took up his fief at Jianchang, the former seat of the Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 性儉約，巾服浣至再，日一素食。

translations.literal: By nature frugal and restrained, he washed his cap and robes twice before wearing them again and ate one vegetarian meal a day.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal by nature, he wore his caps and robes until they had been washed twice and ate only one vegetarian meal a day.

sentences.zh: 好書史，愛民重士，無所侵擾。

translations.literal: He loved books and history, cherished the people and honored scholars, and did nothing to harass them.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and history, treated the people and scholars with respect, and never harassed his domain.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十八年薨。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiajing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing 18.

sentences.zh: 子莊王厚燁嗣，性樸素，外物無所嗜。

translations.literal: His son Prince Zhuang Hou Ye succeeded; by nature plain and simple, he had no craving for external things.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Zhuang Hou Ye succeeded him; plain and unworldly by nature, he cared nothing for luxury.

sentences.zh: 三十五年薨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-fifth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟恭王厚炫嗣，自奉益儉，辭祿二千石。

translations.literal: Having no son, his younger brother Prince Gong Hou Xuan succeeded; he lived all the more frugally and declined two thousand shi of stipend.
translations.idiomatic: With no direct heir, his younger brother Prince Gong Hou Xuan succeeded and lived even more austerely, declining two thousand shi of stipend.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Wanli 5.

sentences.zh: 孫宣王翊鈏嗣，嗜結客，厚炫所積府藏，悉斥以招賓從，通聘問於諸藩，不數年頓盡。

translations.literal: His grandson Prince Xuan Yi Yin succeeded; he loved gathering clients, and all the treasury stores Hou Xuan had accumulated were entirely spent to win followers and send envoys to the other princes; within a few years they were entirely exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Prince Xuan Yi Yin succeeded; addicted to patronage, he spent the entire princely treasury entertaining followers and exchanging envoys with other fiefs until the stores were empty within a few years.

sentences.zh: 三十一年薨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-first year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 子敬王常氵遷嗣，四十三年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Jing Chang Qian succeeded; in the forty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Jing Chang Qian succeeded and died in the forty-third year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 子由本嗣，國亡竄閩中。

translations.literal: His son You Ben succeeded; when the state perished he fled into Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: His son You Ben succeeded; when the dynasty fell he fled into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 衡恭王祐楎，憲宗第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Gong of Heng, You Kai, was the seventh son of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong of Heng, You Kai, was Emperor Xianzong's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年之藩青州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he went to his fief at Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 12 he went to his fief at Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十七年薨。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Jiajing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing 17.

sentences.zh: 子莊王厚燆嗣，嘗辭祿五千石以贍宗室，宗人德之。

translations.literal: His son Prince Zhuang Hou Kai succeeded; he once declined five thousand shi of stipend to support the clansmen, and the kindred were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Zhuang Hou Kai succeeded. He once declined five thousand shi of stipend to support the clansmen, and the kindred were grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Longqing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Longqing 6.

sentences.zh: 子康王載圭嗣，萬歷七年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Kang Zai Gui succeeded; he died in the seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Kang Zai Gui succeeded and died in Wanli 7.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟安王載封嗣，十四年薨。

translations.literal: Having no son, his younger brother Prince An Zai Feng succeeded; he died in the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, his younger brother Prince An Zai Feng succeeded and died in year 14.

sentences.zh: 子定王翊鑊嗣，二十年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Ding Yi Huo succeeded; he died in the twentieth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Ding Yi Huo succeeded and died in year 20.

sentences.zh: 子常㵂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chang Ni succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang Ni succeeded.

sentences.zh: 新樂王載璽，恭王孫也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xinle Zai Xi was a grandson of Prince Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xinle Zai Xi was a grandson of Prince Gong.

sentences.zh: 博雅善文辭，索諸藩所纂述，得數十種，梓而行之。

translations.literal: Learned and elegant, skilled in literary composition, he sought out compilations from the various princedoms, obtained several dozen kinds, and had them printed and circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and elegant and skilled in literary composition, he sought out compilations from the various princedoms, obtained several dozen works, and had them printed and circulated.

sentences.zh: 又撰《洪武聖政頌》、《皇明政要》諸書，多可傳者。

translations.literal: He also authored works such as "Odes to the Sage Governance of the Hongwu Reign" and "Essentials of Imperial Governance of the Great Ming," many of which were worth transmitting.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote works such as "Odes to the Sage Governance of the Hongwu Reign" and "Essentials of Imperial Governance of the Great Ming," many of which were worth preserving.

sentences.zh: 從父高唐王厚煐、齊東王厚炳皆以博學篤行聞。

translations.literal: His father's younger cousins Prince of Gaotang Hou Ying and Prince of Qidong Hou Bing were all famed for broad learning and steadfast conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father's younger cousins Prince of Gaotang Hou Ying and Prince of Qidong Hou Bing were both famed for broad learning and upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，賜敕獎諭者再。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing reign he was twice granted edicts of commendation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign he was twice granted edicts of commendation and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 雍靖王祐枟，憲宗第八子。

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Yong You Cong was the eighth son of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Yong You Cong was Emperor Xianzong's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 初封保寧，弘治十二年之藩衡州。

translations.literal: At first enfeoffed at Baoning, in the twelfth year of Hongzhi he went to his fief at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Initially enfeoffed at Baoning, he took up his fief at Hengzhou in Hongzhi 12.

sentences.zh: 地卑濕，宮殿朽敗不可居，邸中數有異，乞移山東東平州。

translations.literal: The land was low and damp; the palace buildings were rotten and uninhabitable; within the residence strange things occurred repeatedly, and he requested relocation to Dongping in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: The site was low and damp, the palace buildings were rotting and uninhabitable, strange occurrences plagued the residence, and he petitioned to be moved to Dongping in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 廷臣以擇地別建，勞民傷財，四川敘州有申王故府，宜徙居之。

translations.literal: Court ministers held that choosing another site and building anew would burden the people and waste resources; in Xuzhou, Sichuan, there was the former residence of the Prince of Shen, and he ought to be moved there.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers argued that building a new residence would waste public funds; they proposed moving him to the former Prince of Shen's residence at Xuzhou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 既而以道遠不可徙。

translations.literal: Afterward, because the route was too far, relocation could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The move was never carried out because the distance proved too great.

sentences.zh: 正德二年，地裂，宮室壞，王薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde the ground split open, the palace buildings were destroyed, and the prince died.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 2 the earth split open, the palace collapsed, and the prince died.

sentences.zh: 無子，封除。

translations.literal: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: With no heir, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 壽定王祐榰，憲宗第九子。

translations.literal: Prince Ding of Shou You Zhi was the ninth son of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ding of Shou You Zhi was Emperor Xianzong's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年與汝、涇、榮、申四王同日封。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi he was enfeoffed on the same day as the four princes of Ru, Jing, Rong, and Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 4 he was enfeoffed on the same day as the Princes of Ru, Jing, Rong, and Shen.

sentences.zh: 十一年就藩保寧。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he went to his fief at Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he took up his fief at Baoning.

sentences.zh: 正德元年以岐王世絕，改就岐邸於德安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, because the line of the Prince of Qi had ended, he was moved to the former residence of the Prince of Qi at De'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 1, after the Prince of Qi's line died out, he was moved to the former Qi residence at De'an.

sentences.zh: 校尉橫攖市民，知府李重抑之，奏逮重。

translations.literal: Palace guards violently harassed townspeople; prefect Li Zhong restrained them and memorialized that Zhong be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards bullied townspeople; Prefect Li Zhong checked them and was memorialized for arrest.

sentences.zh: 安陸民劉鵬隨重詣大理對簿，重未之識也，訝之。

translations.literal: The Anlu commoner Liu Peng followed Zhong to the Court of Judicial Review to answer the charge; Zhong did not recognize him and was surprised.
translations.idiomatic: Anlu commoner Liu Peng followed Li Zhong to the Court of Judicial Review to face the charges; Li Zhong did not recognize him and was astonished.

sentences.zh: 鵬曰：「太守仁，為民受過，民皆得效死，豈待識乎！」

translations.literal: Peng said: "The prefect is benevolent and bears punishment on the people's behalf; the people may all give their lives for him; why wait to know him!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Peng said: "Our prefect is benevolent and accepts punishment for the people's sake; we would all die for him without needing to know him first!"

sentences.zh: 重卒得白。

translations.literal: Zhong was at last cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong was finally cleared of the charges.

sentences.zh: 祐榰聞而悔之，後以賢聞。

translations.literal: You Zhi heard of this and regretted it; afterward he became famed for worthiness.
translations.idiomatic: You Zhi heard of this and repented; he later won a reputation for virtue.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十四年薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiajing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing 24.

sentences.zh: 無子，除封。

translations.literal: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: With no heir, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 汝安王祐梈，憲宗第十一子。

translations.literal: Prince An of Ru, You Bing, was the eleventh son of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince An of Ru, You Bing, was Emperor Xianzong's eleventh son.

sentences.zh: 弘治十四年之藩衛輝。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongzhi he went to his fief at Weihui.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 14 he went to his fief at Weihui.

sentences.zh: 正德十五年請預支食鹽十年為婚費。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhengde he requested advance allocation of ten years' salt ration for marriage expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 15 he requested ten years' salt ration in advance for marriage expenses.

sentences.zh: 詔別給長蘆鹽二千引，食鹽如故。

translations.literal: An edict granted separately two thousand yin of Changlu salt, while his regular salt allotment continued unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted separately two thousand yin of Changlu salt while his regular salt allotment continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 世宗南巡，迓於途，甚恭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong made his southern tour, You Bing met him on the road with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong made his southern tour, You Bing met him on the road with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 加祿五百石，錫金幣。

translations.literal: He was granted an additional five hundred shi of stipend and bestowed gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an additional five hundred shi of stipend and bestowed gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年薨。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jiajing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing 20.

sentences.zh: 無子，封除。

translations.literal: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.

sentences.zh: 涇簡王祐橓，憲宗第十二子。

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Jing, You Qian, was the twelfth son of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Jing, You Qian, was Emperor Xianzong's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年之藩沂州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi he went to his fief at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 15 he went to his fief at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十六年薨。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiajing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing 16.

sentences.zh: 子厚烇未封而卒。

translations.literal: His son Hou Quan died before receiving a title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hou Quan died before receiving a title.

sentences.zh: 無子，封除。

translations.literal: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.

sentences.zh: 榮莊王祐樞，憲宗第十三子。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang of Rong, You Shu, was the thirteenth son of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuang of Rong, You Shu, was Emperor Xianzong's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 正德初尚留京邸，乞霸州信安鎮田，故牧地也。

translations.literal: In early Zhengde he still remained at his capital residence and requested the fields of Xin'an Township in Bazhou—the former pasture lands.
translations.idiomatic: In early Zhengde he still remained at his capital residence and requested the fields of Xin'an Township in Bazhou, the former pasture lands.

sentences.zh: 部臣言：「永樂中，設立草場，蕃育馬匹，以資武備。

translations.literal: Ministry officials said: "In the Yongle reign pasture grounds were established to breed horses and supply military readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry officials said, "In the Yongle reign pasture grounds were established to breed horses and supply military readiness.

sentences.zh: 至成化中，近幸始陳乞為莊。

translations.literal: By the Chenghua reign favorites first petitioned to have them made private estates.
translations.idiomatic: By the Chenghua reign favorites first petitioned to have them converted into private estates.

sentences.zh: 後岐、壽二府相沿，莫之改正。

translations.literal: Later the Qi and Shou princedoms followed suit, and none corrected this.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Qi and Shou princedoms followed suit, and no one corrected the practice.

sentences.zh: 暨孝宗皇帝留神戎務，清理還屯，不以私廢公也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong attended to military affairs, he reclaimed and restored garrison colonies, not sacrificing public interest to private gain.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong attended to military affairs, he reclaimed and restored garrison colonies, refusing to sacrifice public interest to private gain.

sentences.zh: 今榮王就國有期，所請宜勿與。」

translations.literal: Now that the Prince of Rong has a fixed date to go to his fief, this request should not be granted."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Prince of Rong has a fixed date to go to his fief, this request should not be granted."

sentences.zh: 三年之藩常德。

translations.literal: In the third year he went to his fief at Changde.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he went to his fief at Changde.

sentences.zh: 祐樞狀貌類高帝，居國稍驕縱。

translations.literal: You Shu's appearance resembled the founding emperor; in his princedom he was somewhat proud and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: You Shu's appearance resembled the founding emperor, and in his princedom he was somewhat proud and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔以沅江酉港、天心、團坪河泊稅入王邸。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong ordered that the river-lake taxes of Yuanjiang Xigang, Tianxin, and Tuanping be paid into the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong ordered that the river and lake taxes from Yuanjiang Xigang, Tianxin, and Tuanping be paid into the princely residence.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十八年薨。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiajing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing 18.

sentences.zh: 孫恭王載墐嗣，萬歷二十三年薨。

translations.literal: His grandson Prince Gong Zai Jin succeeded; he died in the twenty-third year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Prince Gong Zai Jin succeeded and died in Wanli 23.

sentences.zh: 子翊鉁嗣，四十年薨。

translations.literal: His son Yi Qin succeeded; he died in the fortieth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi Qin succeeded and died in year 40.

sentences.zh: 子常溒嗣，薨。

translations.literal: His son Chang Ying succeeded and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang Ying succeeded and died.

sentences.zh: 子憲王由枵嗣，薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Xian You Xiao succeeded and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Xian You Xiao succeeded and died.

sentences.zh: 子慈炤嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ci Zhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ci Zhao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 張獻忠入湖南，奉母妃姚氏走辰溪，不知所終。

translations.literal: When Zhang Xianzhong entered Hunan, he fled with his mother Consort Yao to Chenxi; his final fate was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xianzhong entered Hunan, he fled with his mother Consort Yao to Chenxi; his final fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 申懿王祐楷，憲宗第十四子。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Shen You Kai was the fourteenth son of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Shen You Kai was Emperor Xianzong's fourteenth son.

sentences.zh: 封敘州，未就藩。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed at Xuzhou, he never went to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed at Xuzhou, he never took up his fief.

sentences.zh: 弘治十六年薨。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Hongzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Hongzhi 16.

sentences.zh: 無子，封除。

translations.literal: Having no son, the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: With no heir, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝宗二子。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong had two sons.

sentences.zh: 武宗、蔚王厚煒，俱張皇后生。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong and Prince Wei Hou Wei were both born of Empress Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong and Prince Wei Hou Wei were both sons of Empress Zhang.

sentences.zh: 蔚悼王厚煒，孝宗次子，生三歲薨。

translations.literal: Prince Dao of Wei, Hou Wei, was the second son of Emperor Xiaozong; he died at the age of three.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dao of Wei, Hou Wei, was Emperor Xiaozong's second son and died at the age of three.

sentences.zh: 追加封謚。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment and posthumous title were conferred retroactively.
translations.idiomatic: His title and posthumous honors were conferred retroactively.
